This is super cool, @dev2049. Thank you so much for your effort on this! This makes the Vespa retriever much more useful. 

For the cord19 API, where we extend Vespa with more functionality ([app](https://github.com/vespa-cloud/cord-19-search)),  there are several interesting queries you can use to demonstrate this functionality. 

[Sample query request ](https://api.cord19.vespa.ai/search/?query=environmental+impact+due+to+pandemic+travel+restrictions&ranking.profile=colbert&summary=short&restrict=doc&collapse.enable=true&collapse.similarity.threshold=0.85&hits=10)

- Prefer using summary=short as summary=default with "select *" also returns specter_embedding and colbert document embeddings
- Prefer using cord_uid as the id (from within fields)
- You can switch on and off the bolding of terms with `&bolding=false` which might be handy for piping the results into the pipelines. That would probably be an interesting demo to ask questions about covid, powered by retrieval of this API. 

There are also several ranking implementations. 
- `ranking=colbert` multi-vector ranking
- `ranking=hybrid-colbert` combination of bm25 and colbert maxsim
- `ranking=bm25` plain bm25
author: jobergum

body:
Cool stuff @dev2049 💪🏻 

I have a few comments:

---

As suggested by @jobergum in #4008, we should also allow the user to insert [native Vespa embedders](https://docs.vespa.ai/en/embedding.html#embedding-a-query-text). This is an example:

```python
        {
            "yql": "select content from paragraph where userQuery() or {targetHits: 100}nearestNeighbor(embedding, first_query)",
            "query": "Where is Waldo?",
            "input.query(first_query)": "embed(bertModel, Where is Waldo?)",  # <-- This guy here
            "type": "weakAnd",
            "hits": 5,
            "ranking": "documentation",
            "locale": "en-us"
        }
```

One could extend the `from_params` factory with a `native_embedders` `dict` argument:

```python
native_embedders = {
    "first_query": "bertModelOne",
    "second_query": "bertModelTwo",
}

for input_query, embedder in native_embedders.items():
   body[f"input.query({input_query})"] = f"embed({embedder}, {query})"
``` 

---

I think that having both `metadata_fields` and `_filter` might be redundant. Let me try to explain why.
Currently, providing a field inside `metadata_fields` is useful only if then that field is referenced inside `_filter`. I think they could be merged into a `metadata_filters` dictionary which looks like this:

```python
metadata_filters = {
    "title": "contains Japan",
    "year": "> 2023",
}
```

The `metadata_filters` should not be part of the `from_params` factory method but should only be passed to the `get_relevant_documents_with_filter` method.

---

I emphasise that these above are mainly high-level thoughts and I might be wrong 🙏🏻

body:
Hey @Chae4ek! The parameters are needed to set the prompt context correctly. They typically will not require any changes on the user side and as far as I know work well across MPT, llama, and GPTJ models. However, I do think they are nice to have as they may change model behavior (for example, I have messed around with `temp` param at times to see how it impacts the generated text) and they are "technically" required inputs to the C function calls. 

I'm not sure what that `backend` check was for but when loading a GPT4All model using the Python bindings, we will load the correct model. The only case where this isn't applied is if it's a custom model built not provided by us but built off a valid ggml/llama.cpp backend. In this case, providing `model_type` is needed for us to know which architecture to use. Hope this provides some clarification. Let me know if there's anything else I can help with!

body:
@eyurtsev  Hey Eugene, I've made it as a "not breaking change" :) 
Introduced an optional `query` parameter in BaseLoader. In this way, we don't need to add it to the load (and other methods).
If we need a query in method, we can instead do it in two steps: 1) loader_instance.query = query 2) loader_instance.load()
(see an example in BaseLoader.get_relevant_documents():L53-55)
author: leo-gan

body:
> @eyurtsev Hey Eugene, I've made it as a "not breaking change" :) Introduced an optional `query` parameter in BaseLoader. In this way, we don't need to add it to the load (and other methods). If we need a query in method, we can instead do it in two steps: 1) loader_instance.query = query 2) loader_instance.load() (see an example in BaseLoader.get_relevant_documents():L53-55)

Hah! Yeah I get what you're doing -- the current loaders are causing some awkward downstream patterns when implementing the loader. I don't think we're ready yet to tackle a refactor of the base loader or retriever since there are larger changes that we'll probably want to plan for. I suggest we keep the loader as minimal as possible for now; with a sole responsibility of yield a fully partialled function (aka the load method) which can return a list of documents.

In the other PR I shared, I was trying to come up with some way of introducing another type into the hierarchy to enable compositional use, so we produce minimal changes on the BaseLoader. I don't think the pattern I came up with is good since it's introducing a lot of indirection and a lot of extra instantiation. (Perhaps it might have made more sense to create a loader from a retriever rather than a retriever from a loader.) 

We can also keep the arxiv retriever that you had as is for now and collect a few more examples before trying to generalize.

author: eyurtsev

body:
> One concern about behavior is that the pdf paper is used when available and if not falling back silently to the abstract, but the user doesn't have a way of configuring the behavior (e.g., always use abstract, or skip over entries where underlying document isn't available)

I see your point. More control from the user would indeed be better. 
However, I do not know the best way to address this.
My point being, let's say you have an option like `content_source` with choices:
* `abstract` not to look at files and always get the abstract, ok,
* `file_or_abstract`, the current behavior, abstract as a fallback content if not usable file,
*  `file` to retrieve the local pdf files. But what happens, if there is no file or no valid one? Do we want to raise an error, which may be detrimental as in a long list of references, it is highly likely that some would fail. Or do we want to silently go to an empty string or skip this entry, which poses the same problem as the original one.

Is there a defined strategy for similar issues in other loaders?
author: wavefrontshaping

body: @eyurtsev Any thoughts?
author: wavefrontshaping

body:
@wavefrontshaping thanks for the ping! 

We can keep the current auto behavior and enhance with more loading strategies after landing this PR. Not a blocker IMO.

-----

My guess is that users that choose `file` will probably be OK skipping entries were the file cannot be loading (maybe with a potential warning or error logged). However, we could add another file loading strategy that raises on error. Anyway, I think we can add those as needed via the __init__ without causing any breaking changes.

author: vowelparrot

body:
> This is really cool! And thank you for the PR and patience! The reason I'm taking some time to review this is that it changes a couple pretty core pieces - the agent executor and callback managers. While you do an excellent job of making sure it's all compatible, we may want to look into if a lighter-touch implementation would be appropriate here. I think @hwchase17 will have some stronger opinions than I right now in terms of how the agent framework should evolve

Sure! 100% no hurt feelings.

I think we have 2 options:
1. Implement Reflexion as an agent type. Then there's no need for changes in agent executor & callback managers, but we won't be able to use Reflexion with new agent types.
2. Introduce the concept of re-trys. Then we can use Reflexion with any agent type, but this requires changes in agent executor & callback managers.

I went with 2 because @noahshinn024 explicitly stated "Reflexion is not a replacement for [...] any [....] decision-guiding approach! It is a simple retry technique that can be used (to) enhance other approaches."

How would you design a light-version? Am happy to implement :)

Edit: formatting

author: dev2049

body:
Could be, but it does not have to be always the case.
This class in particular has a `init` parameter `pre_delete_collection: bool = False` to delete the collection if it exists, so you can easily "clean" the embeddings of a collection (and the collection itself).
Using the param `pre_delete_collection=True` any operation would trigger the error in the log until the collection exists. It could be avoided checking if the collection exists, but that would imply an extra DB access and adding useless complexity to the code using this library.

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Document:
    page_content: None
    metadata: None

docs = []

    doc = Document(page_content=f'text_{i}', metadata=f'metadata_{i}')

     Document(page_content='text_1', metadata='metadata_1'),
     Document(page_content='text_2', metadata='metadata_2')]



## 4 Proposed methods (the last 2 for completion) 


```python
def function_1(documents):
    texts = [doc.page_content for doc in documents]
    metadatas = [doc.metadata for doc in documents]
    return texts, metadatas

def function_2(documents):
    texts, metadatas = [], []
    for doc in documents:
        texts.append(doc.page_content)
        metadatas.append(doc.metadata)
    return texts, metadatas

def function_3(documents):
    return tuple(zip(*([d.page_content, d.metadata] for d in documents)))

def function_4(documents):
    list_of_pairs = []
    for d in documents:
        list_of_pairs.append([d.page_content, d.metadata])
    return tuple(zip(*list_of_pairs))
```

function_1(docs)

## Comparison across various docs lengths


```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import timeit

list_lengths = [1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000, 10000000]
timings = {'original_function': [], 'proposed_function': [], 'alternate_function': [], 'alternate_function_2': []}
functions = {'original_function': function_1, 'proposed_function': function_2, 'alternate_function': function_3, 'alternate_function_2': function_4}

for length in list_lengths:
    documents = docs[:length]
    for function_name, function in functions.items():
        start_time = timeit.default_timer()
        function(documents)
        end_time = timeit.default_timer()
        timings[function_name].append(end_time - start_time)

for function_name, times in timings.items():
    plt.plot(list_lengths, times, label=function_name)

plt.xlabel('List Length')
plt.ylabel('Time (seconds)')
plt.legend()
plt.loglog()
plt.show()

values = {'generation_info': None, 'text': "J'adore la programmation."}

    @root_validator
    def set_text(cls, values: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
>       values["text"] = values["message"].content
E       KeyError: 'message'
```

With InMemoryCache, test code work fine

```python
langchain.llm_cache = InMemoryCache()
chat = ChatOpenAI(temperature=0, openai_api_key=get_openai_api_key())
messages = [
    SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful assistant that translates English to French."),
    HumanMessage(content="I love programming.")
]
start = time.time()
print(chat(messages))
print(f"first time = {time.time() - start}")
start = time.time()
print(chat(messages))
print(f"first time = {time.time() - start}")
```

My guess is that InMemoryCache is just python dictionary, so it save data as ChatGeneration type. However, SQLiteCache is local database, so it save data as Generation type. If cache hit with SQLiteCache (and other type cache), loaded data is Generation type, not ChatGeneration. So, there is no "message" property in loaded data.
Fast(?) solution is implementing langchain.chat_model seperately, which save and load ChatGeneration type. But, it need two cache code, llm and chat_model for all cache implementation.
To solve this problem, BaseCache need to be modified (I think). But, It is complicated.

  - The code can load GDoc, GSheet, and GSlide documents, or, for other documents, use a dictionary with an association between the mime-type and a loader.
  - A loop loads the first page of `list()` API, extracts some files, and continues with the next pages.
  - Some modifications were applied if the document is a shortcut, or if some documents lack metadata, etc.
  - All [list()](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/reference/files/list) parameters can be set in this class.
  - To initialize the credentials, I propose using an environment variable `GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_FILE`.
  The file can be for a user or a service (I analyze the file to use the correct API).

  - I have implemented the `lazy_load()` and `load()` APIs
  - I propose a tool to update the `description` attribute in GDrive file with a summary of the body of the document (`lazy_update_description_with_summary()` and `update_description_with_summary()`).

We can harness the `self.max_results` to limit the search results, for example:

```python
    for i, res in enumerate(results, 1):
        snippets.append(res['body'])
        if i == self.max_results:
            break

```

`Generator` is much simple:

```python
...
    for i, res in enumerate(results, 1):
        yield res['body']
        if i == self.max_results:
            return
...
```

In the latest version of duckduckgo_search, it is recommand to use context manager with `DDGS`:

```python
with DDGS() as ddgs:

body:
@DvirDukhan 
With current implementation it is not possible to define multiple sentinel instances unfortunately.
It might be possible not using urllib Parser using a comma separated list as host:port names or similar but it does not look right...

### Usage implications
- Using a classic (e.g. bare metal) setup you will have a problem if the one sentinel mentioned within the url is down. 
- Having a load balancer in front of the sentinels (only for the clients) it will work even when one sentinel goes down as all others are reachable with the same DNS name - this kind of setup is quite common using most public helm charts to setup Redis in Kubernetes - there you have a load-balanced DNS name as well as one name per Sentinel. Redis-Clients using the load-balanced name can reach Sentinels all the time to query the current master Redis server. So it is not a problem for HA setups.

Having said this i know this implementation is far from perfect and i am open for enhancements...
Especially i'd like to hear about Redis Labs thoughts for Urls with Sentinels. It would be great to have some authoritive suggestions on that to get common implementations over different languages.

For this PR i tried to get an implementations without changes needed to existing clients and where a Sentinel setup can be used as a drop-in replacement without code changes for everyone using Redis standalone right now - just change the url configuration and you are ready to go.

### Testing
 i have not found test files regarding the Redis connection setup, therefor no changes here. And all current test for Redis standalone must work without changes, nothing needed here.

### Improvements needed
Current PR does not address Sentinel with TLS setup. But i like to address this as well.

Should the TLS Url changed to "rediss+sentinel" similar to Redis standalone? Define TLS via Url parameter?
Shall we support a mixed setup with Redis server or Sentinel using TLS and the other not? Server-side admin can be configure this kind of setup but - at least from my point of view - security wise it is broken and should not be acceptable for clients, So i tend to say either no TLS at all or all connections use TLS.

What are your thoughts about that?

It is used together. In addition, the other three tools all have mutual references. Eg `InfoSQLDatabaseTool` [description](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/langchain/tools/sql_database/tool.py#LL65C1-L65C1) and `QueryCheckerTool` [description](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/langchain/tools/sql_database/tool.py#L118)

author: dev2049

body:
@dev2049 that's interesting. 

In that case, I guess the cleanest way to do this would be to have something like `chroma_id` stuffed into the metadata whenever a `Document` object is passed to `Chroma` or created by `Chroma` (eg `add_texts`) -- and then stripped out before syncing back to Chroma (so the key-value doesn't get written to Chroma). This would mean that metadata in Chroma for an object would not match metadata in the Document, which I think is broadly a con b/c it is harder to reason about. 

The downside of this is that the attribute is ~strictly `read-only` in the sense that users can not set the property on the object, it can only be set for them. EG - it would be fairly obtuse for the user to set the foreign_id themselves in metadata and then have the expectation that to be respected in all operations.

`ids` in Chroma are currently immutable, though this isn't a hard and fast requirement of our API. 

This can also be solved by simply asking the user to maintain their own array of `Tuples` or other to keep track of `foreign_id-Document` pairs. In the long term, this feels like work that the user shouldn't have to do however. 

I totally respect that you are thinking more deeply about it! I mainly raised this PR to start/continue the conversation around this idea. I think I want to avoid workaround "magic" solutions for now, b/c that also will require that users migrate data down the road which is painful for everyone.

In any case - I'll keep PRs that do not require this change while you all consider how to approach it. And we can close this for now. (or keep it open for a few days to attract comments)
author: jeffchuber

body:
A few points for discussion:

* Should documents be immutable? Making them immutable will likely help to prevent a bunch of issues and makes code easier to reason about, but this complicates implementation of the pattern described in the PR.
* Documents could have their own uid assigned based on content hashes of the document. This does not require immutability, but makes more sense if immutability is present.
* What are administration patterns in production applications? Do users retain document objects after writing content into the search engine? Is it possible to phrase administration in terms of the `uid` associated with the documents, so no notion of foreign ids has to be introduced?
* What happens with foreign_id if a user needs to index the documents into multiple systems?

body:
Thanks for the feedback @hwchase17 🙇 

I perhaps should have first pushed an issue for this describing the problem a little more succinctly so my apologies for that! That being said there is currently an Issue in which a few users are starting to flag this [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/issues/2925)  (albeit its a different instance of the same issue - more later!)

The issue here is actually that the way in which the internal `client` attribute is defined is incorrect as per Pydantics docs ( https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/usage/models/#private-model-attributes ). (A more succinct example IMO is listed [here](https://codingshower.com/pydantic-private-fields-or-attributes/)). As a result linters and analysers currently expect that `client` is a required constructor parameter.

We currently don't see this in our linter as the mypy version (0.991) is around 6 months old at this point. However this is currently being flagged by a number of Typing aware linters/static analysers. Pylance is one such example but mypy (any versions > 1.1.1) also flags this (and a number of others) as well:

```bash
langchain-py-env) iceberg ➜ /workspaces/langchain $ mypy --version 
mypy 1.1.1 (compiled: no)
(langchain-py-env) iceberg ➜ /workspaces/langchain $ poetry run mypy tests/integration_tests/embeddings/test_openai.py
langchain/formatting.py:11: error: Argument 1 of "check_unused_args" is incompatible with supertype "Formatter"; supertype defines the argument type as "Set[Union[int, str]]"  [override]
langchain/formatting.py:11: note: This violates the Liskov substitution principle
langchain/formatting.py:11: note: See https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html#incompatible-overrides
tests/integration_tests/embeddings/test_openai.py:11: error: Missing named argument "client" for "OpenAIEmbeddings"  [call-arg]
tests/integration_tests/embeddings/test_openai.py:20: error: Missing named argument "client" for "OpenAIEmbeddings"  [call-arg]
tests/integration_tests/embeddings/test_openai.py:32: error: Missing named argument "client" for "OpenAIEmbeddings"  [call-arg]
tests/integration_tests/embeddings/test_openai.py:40: error: Missing named argument "client" for "OpenAIEmbeddings"  [call-arg]
```
So `client` *must* be renamed to be `_client` as per convention (or this also will be reported as an error).  

It was a great point on that internal Pydantic values assignment though, and one i'd missed. So i've taken another pass and moved to a slightly different initialisation model. I think this presents a few benefits:

 - default initialisation/assignment happens in a slightly more pythonic manner (and not within the Pydantic data validation construct)
 - we can maintain the external `<embedding>.client` interface through the use of the `@property`
 - will now pass type checking
 
The slightly wider ranging question though, as you also point out, is that this pattern exists in a few places (you can check these issues with mypy > 1.1.1). However if we're happy with this general approach to model initialisation i'd be happy to chip away at them in incremental PRs going forwards to reduce risk of regression and/or conflict

author: kacperlukawski

body:
> @c0sogi It's a good idea to switch to the list of points instead of the batch, to make things consistent.
> 
> I'm unsure if we should throw `NotImplementedError` for async in local env. The local mode is not intended to be used in production environments, but it's rather designed for quick experiments. How about displaying a warning, but allowing for an event loop blocking?

The qdrant-client library throws a `NotImplementedError` if it itself uses a Client of a type other than `QdrantRemote`. 
If it is a `QdrantLocal`, that is, if the operation takes place in memory or on disk, it does not support asynchronous operations.
However, in the case of QdrantLocal, it is likely possible to perform asynchronous operations without blocking the event loop as follows.

1. if the type of the QdrantClient is QdrantLocal, print a small warning to the user that gRPC asynchronous operations are not supported.
2. get an already running event loop with `asyncio.get_running_loop()`.
3. Have the sync method run in a new threadpool with something like `loop.run_in_executor(None, self.some_sync_method, ...)` to avoid the eventloop blocking effect.

body:
Modifying `StdoutCallbackHandler` could work, but I wonder if it could cause difficulties in separating functionality, which was why I thought that using an explicitly separate handler could make things clearer to the user.

Specifically, there are four cases the user might want:
1. do not print to stdout, do not print to file
2. print to stdout, do not print to file ([this is the current behavior that `verbose=True` triggers)](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/f75f0dbad6030012470a275bf00f84506cd3469f/langchain/callbacks/manager.py#L863)
3. do not print to stdout, print to file
4. print to stdout, print to file

If we modify `StdoutCallbackHandler` to also print to file if a file is given, this would allows us to handle cases 1, 2, 4. Any suggestions on how we could handle case 3?

If `StdoutCallbackHandler` handles both printing to file and printing to stdout could create ambiguity on the user side with respect to what `verbose=True` would do. If the user simply sets `verbose=True`, the behavior would be that it prints to stdout, but does not write to file. If the user wants to both print to stdout and also write to file, then the user would pass the `StdoutCallbackHandler` in explicitly. This ambiguity might not be a big issue, but just flagging this as a possible concern. What do you think?
author: mbchang

body: UPDATE: I realized that one solution to the above concerns could be for the user to pass in two `StdoutCallBackHandlers`, one with a file and one without a file, to the chain. So I will modify `StdoutCallBackHandlers` to take a file in as an optional input.

On second thought, passing in two `StdoutCallBackHandlers` might not work. This is because when the callbacks are configured, if `verbose=True`, then [this line](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/f75f0dbad6030012470a275bf00f84506cd3469f/langchain/callbacks/manager.py#L857) checks instantiates a new `StdoutCallBackHandler` to log to stdout. But if I pass an `StdoutCallBackHandler` with a file argument, then setting `verbose=True` will not instantiate another `StdoutCallBackHandler` to print to stdout.

We would get the following unexpected behavior below, where setting verbose=True does not result in printing stuff to stdout.

body:
My 2 cents:

I am of the opinion the re-factoring highlights the **small** differences between the SQL dialects, which (currently) is limited to a couple of SQL functions (row limit and timestamp) and the quote character.

Point taken that the need many arise for dialect specific changes. I feel that a localized place to handle cross-cutting concerns makes it easier to maintain code in the long run. Having said that, this refactor **does not** prohibit copy/paste versions of the prompt, although this could also be accomplished using switch-case on dialect. 

An added benefit is that highlighting the dialect nuances in one place will make developers of **all** dialects understand and appreciate the commonalities and differences. For example, dialect differences are immediately clear in below code snippet compared to eyeballing multiple (one per dialect) paragraph-long prompts:

    DUCKDB = ("DuckDB", "LIMIT", "double quotes", '"', "today()")
    GOOGLESQL = ("GoogleSQL", "LIMIT", "backticks", "`", "CURRENT_DATE()")
    MSSQL = ("MS SQL", "TOP", "square brackets", "[]", "CAST(GETDATE() as date)")
    MYSQL = ("MySQL", "LIMIT", "backticks", "`", "CURDATE()")

Cheers.

body:
> what happens if SessionId index already exists?

According to the [docs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes/#create-an-index):

> The [db.collection.createIndex()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex/#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method only creates an index if an index of the same specification does not already exist.

I already use this in other projects (including dotnet ones), this just garantees the index exists, if it's already there Mongo will do nothing. 

From experience, the first times I used indexes in Mongo, I used to manually check from the application if that index already existed, but that just ends up being less optimal since there's more information going between Mongo and the application when it's just unecessary.

body:
Just my opinions here. I've not commit bit & am relatively new to langchain.

> This replaces the usage of the insecure `exec` function with a more secure library called [wasm_exec](https://github.com/Jflick58/wasm_exec) TL;DR: Use `chroot` jails, `wasmtime` and a standalone Python3.11 WASM interpreter to safely execute arbitrary code

100% needed, and thanks!

> Some questions before I officially submit this pr:
> 
> * **How critical is it that we support the execution of code containing 3rd-party dependencies?** The team behind the wasm interpreter I vendor with the library is working on porting `numpy` along with some of the c libs needed to enable broader package support.

It's better to get this in place first, and then worry about 3rd party deps later. The security concern massively outweighs feature depth.

>   * _If it is critical, then how critical is it to support Python versions below 3.11?_ Right now the interpreter does support the use of an existing venv for accessing installed 3rd party deps, but the interpreter is only distributed in 3.11 which means I would either a) have to only support 3.11 b) have a 3rd split in the PythonRepl code base (base, AST, Wasm) or b) try to write some hacky and unpythonic code to try to dynamically create a new 3.11-based venv off of the currently active Python environment.

I also think it's not worth a lot of effort to support power Python versions. (b) & (c) feel like maintenance burdens, and simplicity is important in security-minded components.

sorry for the delay here. high level thoughts:
1. We almost certainly don't want to introduce this as a dependency for the main project
2. We want to support as flexible of python running for prototyping purposes as possible
3. We do not want people to be running this in production

I would suggest the following changes:
1. We will move the current python tools and anything that depends on them into `langchain.experimental` and make that a separate package. This should remove CVEs from core langchain, while also hopefullying making it clear its experimental, and also allowing for prototyping
2. I would encourage the creation of a separate `langchain_python` or the like respository where that uses wasm by default. we'd be happy to support this in a variety of ways (help setting up, help publicizing, help maintaining), but i think we'd prefer it to be a separate repository

body:
The main reason for introducing the `session_id` and attaching it to the documents is to enable more granular and user-specific querying within the same vector store index. 

This is particularly useful in scenarios where the VectorStore is hosted and is being used by multiple users or sessions. By attaching a `session_id` to each document, we can ensure that each session or user is essentially operating within their own 'sub-index' within the larger VectorStore index. 

Furthermore, this change does not affect the existing functionality of the `VectorStoreRetrieverMemory` class and is backward-compatible. Developers can choose to use the session-based version or the original version depending on their needs.

It's a minor change, but I think it serves as a boilerplate template for devs trying to add more session-based vector memory storage for their users. (We use this)

author: hwchase17

body:
For example, we built a chatbot using ChromaDB. We measure the performance of the chatbot in two ways:

1. Does ChromaDB retrieve the correct answers from the document for the query?
2. We manually check the responses of the Language Model (LLM).

To check the responses of ChromaDB, we wrote a script and automated the evaluation using our test set. However, we need to take the embedding of each question separately and perform similarity search on ChromaDB individually. By using this method, we were able to measure performance much faster (42x times) and speed up our work. As our dataset grows over time, it saves us a significant amount of time.

For the future, we have considered the following:
By using a vector scoring system that supports batching and creating an LLM chain, we can batch the incoming message requests to the chatbot and obtain responses. This approach will allow us to receive quick responses when the traffic increases and also avoid exceeding the request per time limit set by OpenAI.

body:
@hwchase17 
Yeap you are right you can do the document formatter part with the compressor pipeline. 
I was having issues getting it working but I just tried it with the merger retriever and works.
I will remove the document formatter part and add some tests.
Here an example on how would look:
```Python

# Define 3 diff collections
client_settings = chromadb.config.Settings(
    chroma_db_impl="duckdb+parquet",
    persist_directory=DB_DIR,
    anonymized_telemetry=False,
)
vxsumall = Chroma(
    collection_name="project_store_all",
    persist_directory=DB_DIR,
    client_settings=client_settings,
    embedding_function=emall,
)
vxsummulti = Chroma(
    collection_name="project_store_multi",
    persist_directory=DB_DIR,
    client_settings=client_settings,
    embedding_function=emmulti,
)
vnosumall = Chroma(
    collection_name="project_store_nosum",
    persist_directory=DB_DIR,
    client_settings=client_settings,
    embedding_function=emall,
)

# Define 3 diff retrievers
ret0 = vnosumall.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity", search_kwargs={"k": 5, "include_metadata": True}
)
ret1 = vxsumall.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity", search_kwargs={"k": 10, "include_metadata": True}
)
ret2 = vxsummulti.as_retriever(
    search_type="mmr", search_kwargs={"k": 10, "include_metadata": True}
)
em_filter2 = EmbeddingsRedundantFilter(embeddings=emall)

# We just pass a list of retrievers.
merger = MergerRetriever(retrievers=[ret0, ret1, ret2])

# And if we want to clean the redundant documents "overlap" between the 3 retrievers.
pipeline_comp = DocumentCompressorPipeline(transformers=[em_filter2])
comp_ret1 = ContextualCompressionRetriever(
    base_compressor=pipeline_comp, base_retriever=merger
)

```

@UmerHA thank you!

> One question: In `stream = StreamingLastResponseCallbackHandler.from_agent_type(agent=AgentType.ZERO_SHOT_REACT_DESCRIPTION)`, why do we need the agent type to initialize this callback?

It is just a convenient shorthand for `StreamingLastResponseCallbackHandler(answer_prefix_phrases=["Final Answer:"])`

We can use this class by custom defining `answer_prefix_phrases` like this

```python
stream = StreamingLastResponseCallbackHandler(answer_prefix_phrases=["Now I know the final answer:"])
```

As in here:

https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/e208414a9ae3cc9a6d84b6ebfe5b2c7e4c0cea77/langchain/callbacks/streaming_last_response_callback.py#L308-L323

---

> Also a suggestion: Consider renaming the class to make this PR backward-compatible. If people are already using FinalStreamingStdOutCallbackHandler, they'll get errors.

@UmerHA  IMO, I prefer to keep both classes as separate files, as each classes serve different purposes.

This introduced unexpected behavior for some retrievers.

Running the `MultiQueryRetriever` [notebook](https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/retrievers/how_to/MultiQueryRetriever).

I no longer see expected logging when running:
```
unique_docs = retriever_from_llm.get_relevant_documents(query="What does the course say about regression?")
len(unique_docs)
```

For `MultiQueryRetriever`, `get_relevant_documents` does a few things (PR [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/pull/6833/files#diff-73c5e56610f556ddc4710db1b9da4c6277b8ffaef6d535e3cf1e1ceb4b22b186)).

E.g., it will run `queries = self.generate_queries(query, run_manager)` and log the queries.

It appears the method name has been changed to `_get_relevant_documents`?

And it now requires some additional args (e.g., `run_manager`)?

AFAICT, `get_relevant_documents` currently will just do retrieval w/o any of the `MultiQueryRetriever` logic.  

If this is expected, then documentation will need to be updated for `MultiQueryRetriever` [here](https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/retrievers/how_to/MultiQueryRetriever) to use `_get_relevant_documents` and supply `run_manager` and explain what `run_manager` is.

body:
Hello, @kacperlukawski, I'm back on this and I would like to share my thought process:
- Since last time I looked at this file in code-base, a lot has changed, and so I began with re-implementing the first part I started with.
- Then, I began on the other part which I didn't implement which is allowing defining multiple vectors at time of injecting documents into QDrant (`from_texts` class method).
- Then, I realised defining `vector_key` at class level prevents `langchain` users from using different vectors in collection as all queries will now use `vector_key` from class, so I moved `vector_key` to `similarity_search` method.
- With that, I replaced `vector_key` from class constructor to `vectors_config`, and used it to check for its truthy value in `similarity_search` in order to raise either of two `ValueError` objects; `QDrant` class was initialised with `vectors_config` but value of `vector_key` wasn't provided, or `vector_key` is provided but it isn't one of the vectors defined in `vectors_config`.

With those changes:
- Users of `QDrant` vector store, can now re-use their current collections with the current data, even if it was originally created outside of `langchain`, with any of the vectors collection was defined with.
- It is possible to create a collection `from_documents` with multiple vectors now.
- Original behaviour is preserved.

That said, I'm yet to figure out the effect of this when `QDrant` class is in chain, as I just made this and tested it as a standalone object, not in a chain.

Am I on a path that is accepted by the project standards?

I'm only a causal observer (not a Langchain user or contributor), but I thought it might be good to drop these links in case you're unaware of the ways that attackers can escape from AST-based Python "sandboxes":

https://hacktricks.boitatech.com.br/misc/basic-python/bypass-python-sandboxes
https://github.com/mahaloz/ctf-wiki-en/blob/master/docs/pwn/linux/sandbox/python-sandbox-escape.md

The strategies in these links aren't exhaustive, but hopefully illustrate that this style of sandboxing makes attacks more complex without defeating them entirely.

body:
Thanks for the PR, @boazwasserman! The PAL chain is indeed unsafe.  It seems you've got enough experience to be aware of the points that @qxcv (thanks for the links btw!) is making. I don't think we could really get to enterprise-level security purely via AST validations, even if that were our main focus.

My inclination is still to add these checks in to make it a bit harder to succeed in a naive prompt injection attack.

If someone were to want to use this chain in production, it ought to be isolated further as well. 

To counter a false sense of security, we could log in the PythonREPL 

```
import logging
import functools

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@functools.cache.lru_cache(maxsize=0)
def warn_once() -> None:
    # Warn that the PythonREPL
    logger.warning("Python REPL can execute arbitrary code. Use with caution.")
```

(called in `run`)
cc @hwchase17

body:
We ended up resolving this issue in a different way, and `langchain` versions since 0.0.247 onward are not vulnerable in this way.

Unfortunately, this fact was not picked up by the various vulnerability databases, so we're in the process of following up on that.

The full details of our fix are [here](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/5923#issuecomment-1696053841) but TL;DR:
- We [removed the offending code from `langchain` entirely](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/8425).
- We moved the code to `langchain-experimental`, which is a package intended for prototyping new ideas before all the edge cases are resolved or any APIs are stabilized. There, we're adding prominent security warnings reminding users to limit the database permissions they grant the credentials used with the chain: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/9867

Thanks for your help and for your patience as we polish up our processes for making our security fixes visible to the security tools used in the community.

body: The problem is that callback handler events are not guaranteed to be non-blocking, for example, they can write to disk or db/make api calls, etc. At some point, we will restrict only using async callback handlers with the async callback manager but until then, we think it's best to run the callback in the event in an executor to avoid blocking the event loop. cc @nfcampos
author: agola11

body:
> we think it's best to run the callback in the event in an executor to avoid blocking the event loop

Sorry for missing that detail. I didn't understand that running in the executor with executor=None would actually run in a different thread. 

> At some point, we will restrict only using async callback handlers with the async callback manager

This is interesting direction.

1. I'm interested in why are you heading this direction. From what I understand, I can write an arbitrary blocking call in a function that's async, and langchain framework can't really know that. So that will force callback authors to have async interface, but inside the interface anything can happen, and you can't really protect users from themselves writing a blocking call inside async function. Is that better than just calling a plain function?


2. From the user perspective (thinking naively), does it mean that I won't be able to call both `generate` and `agenerate` on the same LLM object?

```py
llm = OpenAI(..., callbacks=[my_sync_callbacks])
llm.generate(...)
llm.agenerate(...)
```

Will one of them fail?


----

Why am I looking into it at all?

The main reason I've started looking into this is because I use https://opentelemetry.io/docs/instrumentation/python/ to instrument all LLM requests in the codebase. I think it's become a standard and it might be interesting to you. The setup is pretty much this
- on_llm_start we start a new span and set it as active (active span is kept in contextvar, all handled by open telemetry)
- on_llm_end we end the span.

That worked very well until https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/pull/3256. The reason it stopped working is that each invocation of event handler function gets its own task now (as a consequence of calling gather [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/e0e3ef1c57109ac5491ba744b8e4a4189931b1b5/langchain/callbacks/manager.py#L254-L261)). The actual http call again happens in totally different task (and different contextvar context) again.

Their contextvar contexts look something like this. They all fork from the same context.


```mermaid
graph TD;
    root-->on_llm_start;
    root-->request_1;
    root-->request_n;
    root-->a("on_llm_end");
```

That means that, whatever span on_llm_start marks as "active", it won't matter because the task (and context) will be destroyed. That means that HTTP calls traced can't be assigned to a span started in `on_llm_start` because that context is destroyed, and not shared with requests and on_llm_end handler.

How that means is that if you want to have traces like (imagine first http request failed so we retried)

```py
| -------- llm_request -------|
  |http req 1| |http req 2|
```
you actually can't because no callback can actually set the top llm_request span that will be visible (through contextvars) to the request tasks.

One could think that it's too opentelemetry specific, but I think the issue with the current async hooks design is wider. Anything that uses contextvars and has to share some data between hooks and the requests (through contextvars) will hit the same problem.

We can certainly implement tracing by monkeypatching some methods (either langchain's or clients), but the documentation states that callbacks are useful for tracing and I wanted to expose this implementation issue with the team.

body:
@rlancemartin Is it also the intention for this change to standardize the vector DB ids to be UUIDs? The documentation for the supabase integration ( [python](https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/vectorstores/integrations/supabase) / [javascript](https://js.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/vectorstores/integrations/supabase) ) suggests BIGSERIAL as the type. The underlying database is PostgreSQL with a PGVector extension.

At this moment, if we call the add_documents method, it does not send a list of ids to add_texts method.
```python
base.py:
    def add_documents(self, documents: List[Document], **kwargs: Any) -> List[str]:
        """Run more documents through the embeddings and add to the vectorstore.

        Args:
            documents (List[Document]: Documents to add to the vectorstore.

        Returns:
            List[str]: List of IDs of the added texts.
        """
        # TODO: Handle the case where the user doesn't provide ids on the Collection
        texts = [doc.page_content for doc in documents]
        metadatas = [doc.metadata for doc in documents]
        return self.add_texts(texts, metadatas, **kwargs)

supabase.py:
    def add_texts(
        self,
        texts: Iterable[str],
        metadatas: Optional[List[dict[Any, Any]]] = None,
        ids: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> List[str]:
        ids = ids or [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in texts]
        docs = self._texts_to_documents(texts, metadatas)

        vectors = self._embedding.embed_documents(list(texts))
        return self.add_vectors(vectors, docs, ids)
```

The add_texts method then creates UUIDs and the `upsert` will fail if the table was declared like so:
```sql
-- Create a table to store your documents
create table documents (
  id bigserial primary key,
  content text,
  metadata jsonb,
  embedding vector(1536)
);
```

Any recommendations here?

body:
> this changes existing functionality right?

This PR should not change the existing functionality. It just changes the params for getting pages to expand the `restrictions` property. So we don't need the additional http requests to get the restrictions when checking if the page is public.

The tests fail because the mocked page content has no `restrictions` property.

Related API Reference: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v1/api-group-content/#api-wiki-rest-api-content-get

body:
Thanks @vowelparrot! I have been working on this with Tim. On the high level feedback:

> It's explicitly targeting agents (or rather the agent executor state machine). That's great, I think, especially at first, but I wonder if we want to indicate this in any way via the callback naming since it doesn't support arbitrary "chain" or other workflows.

Yep, we mentioned that in the docstring and would want to call it out in the docs & examples we share too.
* Only concern about changing the name is that we DO want to make it more general later so would that be an annoying name change to deprecate / break in a later version?
* BTW, any ideas on what the right flow / UI would be for this in a non-agent Chain? (like a raw SQLChain or something?) We wracked our brains a bit and weren't totally sure.

> I may be misreading, but it doesn't seem like it supports at most one thought at a time, right? I think that's fine to start, just want to understand the limits a bit here.

I'm not sure I understand what you mean by this, could you share a little more detail or an example of what you mean? The callback integration should support one thought or arbitrarily many thoughts (as seen in the [example app](https://langchain-mrkl.streamlit.app/)). Although one thought / no tool use would render fine but be a bit awkward - related to the chain comment above - very open to ideas on how to support this.

Thank you!

author: tconkling

body:
@vowelparrot (and cc @sfc-gh-jcarroll) - I'm removing the draft status from this PR, and would love another review if you have a chance.

Some notes:
- There's a few unit tests for the "auto-upgrading callback handler" feature that pulls StreamlitCallbackHandler from the streamlit package itself, if it has a newer version of the callback handler
- There's a very basic integration test for the handler. It just runs the "Who is Olivia Wilde's boyfriend" agent query that I saw used in other tests. Obviously, this test requires network access, but:
  - I wrote a (very simple!) tool for testing CallbackHandlers that saves an Agent's callback invocations to a pickle file, and lets you "replay" those callbacks against any set of CallbackHandlers without hitting the network (or spending your token budget). If this would be useful, I'd be happy to add it to the PR and use it in the integration test. (It's just a single small Python file.)
- Re: naming - happy to rename this to `StreamlitAgentCallbackHandler` or whatever you think is appropriate; just let me know and I'll push the change.

Thanks!
author: tconkling

body: Will review in an hour!
author: vowelparrot

body:
@sfc-gh-jcarroll I think this looks good as is, and with the current name. 

In terms of other non-agent flows that are common - I'd say:
-  Some fixed retrieval -> response synthesis for Q&A or summarization, so map reduce chain, SQL DB chain 
- Information extraction
- Some of the experimental agents (BabyAGI, Generative agents, etc.)

You know your users better than I, so maybe the first two are less important for visualizing in streamlit. Perhaps verifying this works reasonably well with custom agents that don't use the existing agent executor would be good, even if it doesn't impact this PR directly
author: vowelparrot

body:
Awesome!! Anything else needed on our end before this can be merged and released?

We will give those other workflows a try and see what viz makes sense with this callback handler in Streamlit (future work). Thank you!!

body:
This score implementation affects similarity_search_with_relevance_scores(base.py).
In _similarity_search_with_relevance_scores(base.py), score value change by relevance_score_fn and check scores. faiss.py and base.py uses same 'score_threshold' value.

In similarity_search_with_score_by_vector(faiss.py), original score value is checked by 'score_threshold'.
But in similarity_search_with_relevance_scores(base.py), score value changed by relevance_score_fn is checked by the same 'score_threshold'.

So, if call similarity_search_with_relevance_scores, score value filtering is processed twice on different criteria before and after conversion.
author: tak-s

body:
> > wont we want to include additional_kwargs?
> 
> @hwchase17 none of the other elements of that function add `additional_kwargs` besides the `function_call` in the `AIMessage` conversion. It's not clear to me what we would even add to `additional_kwargs` in the `FunctionMessage` case.
> 
> Here's the example code from OpenAI, looks like passing a function message is just the `role`, `name`, and `content` to me:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "model": "gpt-3.5-turbo-0613",
>   "messages": [
>     {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather like in Boston?"},
>     {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "function_call": {"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": "{ \"location\": \"Boston, MA\"}"}},
>     {"role": "function", "name": "get_current_weather", "content": "{\"temperature\": "22", \"unit\": \"celsius\", \"description\": \"Sunny\"}"}

body:
I just encountered this with version 3.6.5. Version check has not been updated, and is inconsistent as well. I.e., in deeplake.py, 127-132:

```
version = deeplake.__version__
if version != "3.6.2":
       raise ValueError(
            "deeplake version should be = 3.6.3, but you've installed"
             f" {version}. Consider changing deeplake version to 3.6.3 ."
        )
```
(This check will fail if version is 3.6.3!)

Suggestion (tested on my local installation):

1) define minimum_version globally, e.g., about line 23:

```
minimum_version = "3.6.3"
```

2) Modify version check to:

```
version = deeplake.__version__
if not version >= minimum_version:      
       raise ValueError(
            f"deeplake version should be >= {minimum_version}, but you've installed"
            f" {version}. Consider changing deeplake version to {minimum_version} or later ."
        )
```

3) Update one line of code when updating version, if necessary.

body:
> why cant you just pass in `ids` using the keys variable? they seem pretty overlapping in functionality?

Thanks for the comments!. Not sure if I understood correctly, but if you meant to let users define `ids` inside `keys` parameter, I don't think users should care about the Redis key semantics. Instead, the semantics of `ids` remain as just identifiers instead of governing the index scheme inside Redis. 

Redis keys are generated [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/22601b0b6323e6465f78ca9bc16152062a2b65ba/langchain/vectorstores/redis.py#L78) whose prefix is generated [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/22601b0b6323e6465f78ca9bc16152062a2b65ba/langchain/vectorstores/redis.py#L85). In Redis, those prefixes or namespaces are used as a primary index key and users should not arbitrarily define it without understanding those. For example, users can define keys not conforming [the index defined in the Redis object](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/langchain/vectorstores/redis.py#L134). I argue custom IDs should not affect any indexing scheme.

Among many others, AnalyticDB has [`ids` argument](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/22601b0b6323e6465f78ca9bc16152062a2b65ba/langchain/vectorstores/analyticdb.py#L128) that users can arbitrarily define.

In fact, I think the best solution for this is for langchain to hide `keys` concept at Redis because namespaces, which are indices in langchain, should be considered to be databases or tables in traditional databases, and custom IDs should be agnostic to those (which should be an ID to an entry in a table, etc.)

I don't know the policy to make a breaking change, so I allowed both `keys` and `ids` but I strongly believe `keys` should not be exposed in the functions.

Thanks for the reply! 

Correct. Because we define "index" per Redis instance, I'd argue index-specific prefixes should be abstracted and the end users should rely only on ids (suffixes of the keys). I shouldn't be able to add a key whose index (prefix) is different from the one defined within the scope of the instance.

body:
> @jbkoh is this still relevant for you? Can you not just override the key name with Id's? am I missing something here or can we close this?

Hi @Spartee. I understand we can override the keys, but I was arguing in this PR that we should abstract away the key structure of the Redis. IDs should only mean the customizable part of the key while the whole key exposes the indexing structure in Redis which should not be controlled at this API.
author: jbkoh

body:
I do see what you mean. But I disagree that the indexing should be at that level of abstraction. Provided some concrete examples in which that is of some benefit, I'm happy to reconsider. 

Tagging @baskaryan for his opinion
author: Spartee

body:
I'm lazy to write actual code for now but here are a few immediate cases
- The ID structures are different from other vector store interfaces in LangChain, and it reduces the compatibility with other vector stores while LangChain is supposed to standardize them all.
  - From Redis's customer management perspective, I guess it'll increase the bar to adopt LangChain compared to the others.
- I want to index each page of PDF and want to update vector each when I change the embedding scheme. I don't know the key structure (I mean as a human I know it, but the code structure is not supposed to expose the key structure in the current LangChain flow.) Basically, a controlled ID per PDF/page#.

body:
> @CameronVetter integrated in #6843 relying only on the metadata dictionary for additional fields. It supports also custom index creation directly within LangChain.

I'm not sure I agree with copy/pasting this bug fix into a larger feature PR when this valid and simple PR is ready to merge. It would have been better to get this fix in quickly for the people waiting for it when it was ready last week...  I suppose as long as it gets into the code base ASAP...
author: CameronVetter

body:
> > @CameronVetter integrated in #6843 relying only on the metadata dictionary for additional fields. It supports also custom index creation directly within LangChain.
> 
> I'm not sure I agree with copy/pasting this bug fix into a larger feature PR when this valid and simple PR is ready to merge. It would have been better to get this fix in quickly for the people waiting for it when it was ready last week... I suppose as long as it gets into the code base ASAP...

First, this is not a bug fix. Second, this is not copy/pasting as you are using an additional field instead of relying on the metadata dictionary which is already part of the standard LangChain document structure. Also, not giving the ability to add extra fields in the index definition as per this PR creates the need to work outside of the framework to add additional fields, which is not ideal.
author: ruoccofabrizio

body:
> > > @CameronVetter integrated in #6843 relying only on the metadata dictionary for additional fields. It supports also custom index creation directly within LangChain.
> > 
> > 
> > I'm not sure I agree with copy/pasting this bug fix into a larger feature PR when this valid and simple PR is ready to merge. It would have been better to get this fix in quickly for the people waiting for it when it was ready last week... I suppose as long as it gets into the code base ASAP...
> 
> First, this is not a bug fix. Second, this is not copy/pasting as you are using an additional field instead of relying on the metadata dictionary which is already part of the standard LangChain document structure. Also, not giving the ability to add extra fields in the index definition as per this PR creates the need to work outside of the framework to add additional fields, which is not ideal.

Looking at the overall code structure it sure seems like a lot of the design for this was intended functionality that was missed in the original implementation, thus my calling it a bug.  I could see the argument for it being though, I initially didn't classify it as a bug and only thought of it as one later.

The creation of the index as a side effect of trying to use a vector store that is not there is not desirable, and runs against the pattern of all of the other vector store implementations within langchain, so I'm not sure that adding even more to that is going in the right direction.  I think it would be better to remove that completely and instead give examples of how to create the example and follow already established patterns.

Agreed, using metadata is an improvement.  In the spirit  of getting this merged I'm closing this.  See #6843

body:
Nice work! Interesting PR. 

Suggestion: we can re-organize the code slightly to fit into a `loader` -> `parser` workflow as we do [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/docs/extras/modules/data_connection/document_loaders/integrations/youtube_audio.ipynb).

(1) You should be able to use existing `FileSystemBlobLoader` [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/langchain/document_loaders/blob_loaders/file_system.py) to load the .js or .py files. No new code should be required for loading.

(2) Then, just move your parsing logic into a new parser file in the directory [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/tree/master/langchain/document_loaders/parsers).

The UX is simple and we reduce code duplication (no new loading code). Specifically, the UX can follow what we do [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/master/docs/extras/modules/data_connection/document_loaders/integrations/youtube_audio.ipynb) where the loader and parser are called:

```
# Transcribe the videos to text
loader = GenericLoader(YoutubeAudioLoader(urls, save_dir), OpenAIWhisperParser())
docs = loader.load()
```

In this case, of course it will look like:
```
# Parse js or py to docs
loader = GenericLoader(FileSystemBlobLoader(path="",glob=""), <New_Code_Parser>())
docs = loader.load()
```

Thoughts?
author: rlancemartin

body:

Let me refactor the code.

Nice! Yes, clean UX:

```
loader = GenericLoader.from_filesystem(
    "./example_data/languages",
    glob="*",
    suffixes=[".py", ".js"],
    parser=LanguageParser()
)
docs = loader.load()
```

Small clarification in the docs: 

1) it will default split on classes and functions? can this be configured (e.g., only split on functions)?
2) will the `top-level code, but without the already loaded functions and classes` doc always be generated?

This is looking good. I think we only need to clarify usage a bit. 

In short, it simply looks like this will by default split any js or py based on class and function definitions?

Exactly, it only splits, or segments, the source code based on top-level classes and functions, and the remaining code.

I've edited the documentation trying to make it more straightforward. Also, the docstring mentions the only parameters that can be configured: `language` and `parser_threshold`.

Should I add an example in the notebook like the one I mention in the first post in this PR? I thought that the code and the results would be self-explanatory, but perhaps it's not clear enough.

body:
Hi @raymond-yuan, the metric scores may differ between the databases, for example, pgvector returns the negative of maximum inner product while chroma will return a positive value for this metric, so the normalization/ scaling function should match the database.
I think the default **relevance_score_fn** should be left unimplemented in base for the specific vector store to implement. Besides that I think it is a necessary refactor and a great job in #6570.
I have two pull requests that include related code - this one and #6475. Those versions are working well and the normalization functions I added for chroma and pgvector are tested.
You want to take my chroma and pgvector normalization functions to your pull request and I will resolve the conflicts and match my PRs to the new code? Or the other way around when I merge my changes and the refactor will be done after?
Let me know.
author: hanit-com

body:
>  default relevance_score_fn should be left unimplemented in base

~~I think this should be fine right? We let the vector store define whatever relevance score in `_select_relevance_score_fn` and we rely on that function in `_similarity_search_with_relevance_scores` or maybe I'm misunderstanding your point?~~

gotcha, will revert those changes - i think euclidean and cosine should be standard across all? wdyt
edit: actually, i think we should keep it in the base class- these should be standard across vector stores - instead we can do somehting like:
```
    def _max_inner_product_relevance_score_fn(distance: float) -> float:
        """Normalize the distance to a score on a scale [0, 1]."""
        if distance > 0:
            return 1.0 - distance
    
        return -1.0 * distance
```
wdyt to handle score values 

> You want to take my chroma and pgvector normalization functions to your pull request and I will resolve the conflicts and match my PRs to the new code? Or the other way around when I merge my changes and the refactor will be done after? Let me know.

Either way works! I think maybe the easiest approach would be to merge your changes in to my PR since it is a bit of a superset of changes? Let me know if you want me to go ahead and merge the two PRs into mine
author: raymond-yuan

body:
I like this suggestion, nevertheless, each vector DB returns a different formula, there might be vectorstore that will return the inner product already normalized or return (1.0 - max_inner product). It is a broad subject to resolve in one pull request so I think it is better to handle it in vector store level while keeping each vector store's normalization function as it was.
The centralized normalization functions solution can work if you are confident about it, and it might require adjusting the tests to match the new scores (if changed).
It is also a good thing the user can provide his own implementation in case we got it inaccurately.
About the pull requests, if it works for you then sure, you can merge them into yours!
author: hanit-com

body:
I think it's good to provide some default functions because most of the implementations are standardized. The current implementation does not prevent users from specifying different relevance functions for specific vectorbases, for example one could directly pass the score through the _select_relevance_score_fn without normalizing it if the db has already done this. As of now all of the normalization functions work with the tests as is. We could potentially move the centralized functions into vectorstores/utils, but in either case because so many implementations rely on relatively standard functions, i think providing some default functions for the relevance functions helps a lot with code duplication. 

I went ahead and merged your changes in to my PR (and handled conflicts)!

body:
> we had it like this before but got feedback from other folks that ecosystem was a confusing grouping. maybe we wait to gather more feedback?

I agree that "Ecosystem" is a too broad term and hence confusing. 
Still, [PyTorch uses this term](https://pytorch.org/ecosystem/). 

This PR is a trade-off between moving "Additional resources" items into "Ecosystem" or opposite, moving "Ecosystem" items into "Additional resources". The latter doesn't work because "YouTube" and "Gallery" can be part of the "Ecosystem" but the "Integrations" cannot be part of the "Additional resources". So, decision was to move "YouTube" and "Gallery" into the "Ecosystem". 

How about renaming "Ecosystem" to "Resources" (as [in PyTorch again](https://pytorch.org/resources/))? 

BTW @hwchase17 insisted on "Ecosystem" vs "Integrations" the last time.

body: @raymond-yuan I see tests for chroma, faiss, pgvector, singlestore. but a larger set of DBs (pinecone, etc) are modified; tests for some like pinecone are tricky b/c they are not in memory, but do we have confirmation (e.g., from user testing) that this is a no-op / backwards compatible across the broader set of DBs? i see the the existing logic is moved to `_select_relevance_score_fn`, so it **should** be, but would be nice to verify it we could (e.g., a subtle change in scoring may confuse folks).
author: rlancemartin

body:
> @raymond-yuan I see tests for chroma, faiss, pgvector, singlestore. but a larger set of DBs (pinecone, etc) are modified; tests for some like pinecone are tricky b/c they are not in memory, but do we have confirmation (e.g., from user testing) that this is a no-op / backwards compatible across the broader set of DBs? i see the the existing logic is moved to `_select_relevance_score_fn`, so it **should** be, but would be nice to verify it we could (e.g., a subtle change in scoring may confuse folks).

@rlancemartin added some additional tests (using personal api keys), for additional dbs. To be clear, for vectorstores that already had the relevancy score function already implemented, these should be no-ops and completely backwards compatible. However for the majority of classes that did not have these implemented, the `_similarity_search_with_relevance_scores` will produce different results, whch is the desired outcome since these were incorrectly implemented before (since the old behavior was just doing a similarity search and returning the corresponding distance).

author: olegshirokikh

body:
I found the `score_threshold` also filters out the most relevant doc for the FAISS vectorstore. I think there are still bugs with this refactoring changes. `

First, the `FAISS.similarity_search_with_score` /`similarity_search_with_score_by_vector`  actually returns the score which already represents the similarity score instead of distance... (I validated with the `embed_function` with the same sentences and the dot product is 1 which matches the score from the function) but somehow the docstring says the lower score means more similarity? 

Second, the `_max_inner_product_relevance_score_fn`  should just return the score itself for FAISS (at least) if the higher score from `FAISS.similarity_search_with_score` /`similarity_search_with_score_by_vector` represents the higher similarity... let me know if I miss anything.   

I guess a fix is to implement the `_max_inner_product_relevance_score_fn` in the `FAISS` vectorstore file, like `lambda x: x`.

Let me know what you think! I'll probably close this later this week if it's ok with you because this PR doesn't seem very active anymore :)

body:
> i think probably not ideal to have every document loader inherit from this, maybe we can make a mixin though? only for document laoders which actually have a query param

If the document loader doesn't explicitly define the `query` parameter, it defaults to `everything`. If some document loaders also defined `query`, as `MaxComputeLoader` did, this `query` has the same semantics, so no braking change.
That's the idea, to allow every document loader to inherit the retriever functions.

body: One added point: currently any `parser` accept blobs and inherits from `BaseBlobParser`. In this case, it seemed easier to move your parser code into a new text splitter rather than modify your loader to yield blobs (since you do some processing and produce XML data). Open to feedback from others and will discuss w/ @eyurtsev when he is back from travels. IMO this is something we need to clarify in the documentation (specifically, differences between `loaders -> splitters` vs `blob loaders -> blob parsers`).
author: rlancemartin

body:
I went with option (1) mentioned in code above.

use a existing blob loader to load PDFs and add all the logic (XML generation) to the globid blob parser.

pro: 
+ simplifies the code by consolidating all logic into the parser (rather than separated btwn loader+parser)
+ re-uses existing blog loader for flexibility 
+ avoids adding bloat in text_splitter
+ UX is consistent w/ [recent context aware splitters](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/pull/6486) 

UX:
```
loader = GenericLoader.from_filesystem(
    "./example_data/source_code",
    glob="*",
    suffixes=[".pdf"],
    parser= GrobidParser(segment_sentences=True)
)
docs = loader.load()
```

will add better documentation to help contributors recognize this.

body:
```
chat = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo-16k",temperature=0,callbacks=[StreamingStdOutCallbackHandler()])
prompt_template = """
下面以一篇文章的局部内容，你要为这个局部内容做个不损失重要信息的局部思维导图
这个思维导图要内容层次分明，能突出当前内容的主要信息
以markdown的格式输出答案
-----------------
{text}
-----------------
"""


PROMPT = PromptTemplate(template=prompt_template, input_variables=["text"])
combine_prompt_template = """
下面是一篇文章思维导图，你需要将这些信息进行汇总重构，生成一份新的格式优美的思维导图
要求新的思维导图，内容之间的关联性做到层次丰富，结构合理，不丢失重要信息，去除重复信息
以markdown的格式输出答案
-------
{text}
-------
"""
combine_prompt = PromptTemplate(
            input_variables=["text"],
            template=combine_prompt_template,)
chain_one = load_summarize_chain(chat, chain_type="map_reduce",return_intermediate_steps=True,verbose=True, map_prompt=PROMPT, combine_prompt=combine_prompt)
```


In this code snippet, I utilized mp-reduce to generate a mind map for an article. During the map phase, there were two instances where the token output from a large model exceeded 3000, triggering a ValueError 'A single document was so long it could not be combined'. I believe that when using the gpt-3.5-turbo-16k model, it would be more reasonable to have a larger token_max value instead of 3000. I resolved this error by making the necessary modifications, but it is specific to the gpt-3.5-turbo-16k model. Different models may require different values for token_max.

> this is awesome @yarikoptic! looks like the new codespell CI check is failing :')

someone was too active in master while having no codespell I see ;)   I have now

- discarded prior run of codespell commit 
- adjusted config to ignore more  (see recent commits for details)
- rebased on top of master
- reran codespell

so should be all green if ran/considered now! ;)

> could we add a make command or script to make it easy to run codespell locally?

need more *input*, since I bet you do not really need a script like

```bash
#!/bin/bash
codespell "$@"
```
right? ;)  the point is that running `codespell` is sufficient if you have it installed "properly" (given that config is in pyproject.toml you need `tomli` installed too).

body:
> Distance-based vector database retrieval embeds (represents) queries in high-dimensional space and finds similar embedded documents based on "distance". But, retrieval may produce difference results with subtle changes in query wording or if the embeddings do not capture the semantics of the data well. Prompt engineering / tuning is sometimes done to manually address these problems, but can be tedious.
> 
> The `MultiQueryRetriever` automates the process of prompt tuning by using an LLM to generate multiple queries from different perspectives for a given user input query. For each query, it retrieves a set of relevant documents and takes the unique union across all queries to get a larger set of potentially relevant documents. By generating multiple perspectives on the same question, the `MultiQueryRetriever` might be able to overcome some of the limitations of the distance-based retrieval and get a richer set of results.

@rlancemartin great idea, thanks! Is it possible to combine this with ConversationalRetrievalChain by replacing question_generator prompt with yours that generates multiple questions based on user's question and chat history?

body:
> self.relevance_score_fn is relevant for _similarity_search_with_relevance_scores

Hi @hwchase17 , as I agree that self.relevance_score_fn is majorly used for _similarity_search_with_relevance_scores function but it is also effecting this stage as well. 

Consider the following scenario where we have a vectorstore built out of FAISS vectorstore: 

1. We get the retriever as retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever() which is mostly used for conversational chains. 
2. Given that the search type is set to "similarity_score_threshold", when we call retriever.get_relevant_documents(query) by setting the score threshold to say 0.8, the following workflow is triggered chronologically. (Let us keep in mind that 0.8 threshold set here is the threshold set on the basis of a score of 0 to 1 which ideally is the output of relevance_score_fn.

The steps called are: 

-      self.vectorstore.similarity_search_with_relevance_scores is triggered with the threshold of 0.8 (Line 410 File langchain.vectorstore.base)
-      The next step involves calling self._similarity_search_with_relevance_scores (Line 156 File langchain.vectorstore.base)
-      Function _similarity_search_with_relevance_scores is called from file langchain.vectorstore.faiss which in turn calls self.similarity_search_with_score function with the same query and the same threshold of 0.8
-     Function similarity_search_with_score is called which in turn calls self.similarity_search_with_score_by_vector with the same query and threshold of 0.8
-     self.similarity_search_with_score_by_vector is called with the threshold of 0.8 and the query. This function first fetches the docs till line 229 of langchain.vectorstore.faiss and then gets the score_threshold set which is still 0.8 in this case. It then matches and filters according to the threshold which is 0.8. 
- The score returned in the list docs with the similarities is not between 0 and 1 and thus comparing it to 0.8 will essentially not fetch any results. For example a score of 0.312 in the docs list similarity is actually 0.779 by using the function converter **1.0 - 0.312 / math.sqrt(2)** which is why we need to first convert the similarity score fetched by docs and then compare it to the incoming threshold.

body:
Your approach over mine allows the following:
- Add new documents to QDrant collection that uses a single vector key `vector_name`.
- Query QDrant collection that uses any number of vector keys, using one pre-specified `vector_name`.

My approach in my second PR #5975 allows both scenarios but expands first to allow adding documents to collections that define multiple vector keys.

Now, my use case is already fulfilled with your work, because my use of `langchain` doesn't involve getting it to add new documents, but only for querying them. However, I would like you to understand the difference between both before you finalise your approach.

Nice addition! As mentioned by @dev2049 we should updated the base VectorStore delete class [here](https://github.com/hwchase17/langchain/blob/9ca1cf003cec61db147b2b473e71f82c974abe9c/langchain/vectorstores/base.py#L51) and above suggestion is reasonable to me. 
```
delete(self, ids: Optional[List[str]]=None, **kwargs: Any) 
```

A number of vectorstores have delete methods w/ ids passed, and this would of course be backwards compatible. But making IDs optional is more flexible for future additions, like the nice one you propose here.

body:
> Discussing w/ @nfcampos and @jacoblee93 who are adding this same functionality to js - there is possible confusion if a user passes both filter params and IDs. In this case, ID-wise delete is done first. Thoughts on having independent methods delete_by_id and delete_by_filter? Pinecone simply has delete as done here, so perhaps separate methods also has drawbacks. https://docs.pinecone.io/reference/delete_post

There could also be additional one-off options for other vector stores in the future - if we do separate methods we can always refactor to a single combined one if there's confusion.
author: jacoblee93

body:
the pinecone [doc](https://docs.pinecone.io/reference/delete_post) says that "If specified, the metadata filter here will be used to select the vectors to delete. This is mutually exclusive
with specifying IDs to delete in the ids param or using delete_all=True."
so we can just have the pinecone delete function with ids optional and kwargs, and have some validation in delete function of the pinecone class. what do you say? @rlancemartin
author: 0xcha05
