author: hwchase17

body:
I believe the way of parsing @grabbou suggests makes sense for Claude, but it does not go in line with the general idea of output parsers which should return **structured** response for any given model. The way it is implemented now, we get structured response every time and can modify it later on according to our needs. Also, as it is shown in the notebook, we can ommit parsing, and leave the output as an XML string.

@grabbou if these changes do not address your issue, then I think it should be developed in a separate PR :raised_hands:
author: mateusz-wosinski-ds

body:
In my opinion it would be good to have both and at first glance and with current implementation and design it seems lines 28-29 contain the logic which changes str into dict (please correct me if I am wrong and string output differs for input to parse as XML). I dislike idea of doing unnecessary work and conversion.  As I see it now, to dict operation looks like an adapter.

I see a few solutions:

**a) Keep XMLOutputParser and have a param to determine return type**
However above are non-standard behavior as rather my understanding the design is that parser has clearly defined output type.

**b) have an adapter function/method parse_to_dict() /to_dict or similar**
This is opt-in but results in discoverability issue, as it might be "surprising" for developers. Potentially string_xml_to_dict is reusable in other scenarios (but not sure if any..)

**c) distinct parsers - it is not much work really.**

`XMLOutputParserIntoString` it could be a base class or just implementation detail for `XMLOutputParserIntoDict` which can reuse the first parsing behavior.
It is easy to add output as list etc, typing is verbose and clear.
Maybe the name should be also more like DictFromXMLOutputParser idk. The downside of course is that runtime output format change is not easy and more verbose naming, plus tiny bit of additional work.

Personally I think option c would be the best as it gives more power to end users - what do you think?

body:
Hey, I stumbled upon this, because I had the need to have a local transforms chat pipeline myself. I wrote something similar (but more basic), because I did not find anything in the package. Of course I should have checked ongoing pull requests first before start implementing something myself. ^^

However, I like what you did @eryk-dsai , but wonder if it would be better to leverage the given `HuggigFacePipeline` implementation from `langchain_community`, to avoid double and deviant code. That is, the chat implementation would be more kind of a wrapper. That would seem logical to me, because in the end it does not provide anything else than incorporation of the huggingface chat templates. It is done this way in `langchain_community`multiple times e.g. for `ChatHuggingFace` and `HuggingFaceTextGenInference`, `HuggingFaceEndpoint`, `HuggingFaceHub`. 

E.g. like this (basic example of the concept):
```
class ChatHuggingFacePipeline(SimpleChatModel ):

    llm: HuggingFacePipeline # no direct transformers pipeline, but given HuggingFacePipeline implementation

    def __init__(self, **kwargs: Any):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def _call(
        self,
        messages: List[BaseMessage],
        stop: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        run_manager: Optional[CallbackManagerForLLMRun] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> str:
        
        messages = langchain_to_transformers_msgs(messages)
        input = self.llm.pipeline.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False)

        out = self.llm._generate([input], stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager, **kwargs)

        return out.generations[0][0].text
    
    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        """Return type of chat model."""
        return "huggingface_pipeline_chat_wrapper"
```

So, leaving the pipeline instantiation etc. on transformers level to the `HuggingFacePipeline`class.

One more suggestion from my point one view: One reason I found this PR (to) late is, that I checked for such an implementation in `langchain_community`, because `HuggingFacePipeline` is there, as well as all the other huggingface stuff (`ChatHuggingFace` etc.) So I am wondering if this should be moved to `langchain_community` as well, for consistency.

Was thinking the exact same thing haha

Yeah take look:

langchain.schema.output_parser.OutputParserException: Could not parse tool
input: {'name': 'python', 'arguments': "import pandas as pd\nimport
matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n# Calculate total sales by
month\ndf['ORDERDATE'] = pd.to_datetime(df['ORDERDATE'])\ndf['MONTH_YEAR']
= df['ORDERDATE'].dt.strftime('%b-%Y')\ntotal_sales_by_month =
df.groupby('MONTH_YEAR')['SALES'].sum().reset_index()\n\n# Sort by
month-year\ntotal_sales_by_month['MONTH_YEAR'] =
pd.to_datetime(total_sales_by_month['MONTH_YEAR'],
format='%b-%Y')\ntotal_sales_by_month =
total_sales_by_month.sort_values('MONTH_YEAR')\n\n# Create Combo
Chart\nfig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))\n\n# Bar
Chart\nax1.bar(total_sales_by_month['MONTH_YEAR'],
total_sales_by_month['SALES'],
color='tab:blue')\nax1.set_xlabel('Month/Year')\nax1.set_ylabel('Total
Sales')\nax1.set_title('Monthly Sales Comparison')\n\n# Line Chart\nax2 =
ax1.twinx()\nax2.plot(total_sales_by_month['MONTH_YEAR'],
total_sales_by_month['SALES'], color='tab:red',
marker='o')\nax2.set_ylabel('Total Sales')\n\n# Rotate x-axis
labels\nplt.xticks(rotation=45)\n\n# Save the
figure\nplt.savefig('monthly_sales_comparison.png')\n\n# Show the
figure\nplt.show()"} because the `arguments` is not valid JSON.

And this happens very often when the message that is trying to pass refers
to python code in this case.


On a more general note:

Problem:
The value in function_call['arguments'] is sometimes received as a string, and sometimes it might be expected to be a JSON-formatted string (or another data structure). When the value is a regular string (as in the given case where it's Python code), using json.loads() directly will result in a JSONDecodeError because the string isn't valid JSON.

Solution:
To handle both cases (where function_call['arguments'] might be a regular string or a data structure), the solution first uses json.dumps() to ensure the data is serialized as a JSON string. If the arguments value is already a string, this essentially wraps the string in quotes, making it a valid serialized JSON string.

After the serialization, json.loads() is then used to decode the data back to its original form. In the case of a regular string, it'll just remove the outer quotes, leaving the string as-is. If it was a JSON-formatted string, it would deserialize it to the corresponding Python object.

input: {'name': 'python', 'arguments': "import pandas as pd\nimport
```

The LLM is trying to invoke a 'python' function which was never really a part of the "functions" parameter in the first place (pandas agent only gets PythonAstREPLTool on the tool set - agents/agent_toolkits/pandas/base.py - which is named 'python_repl_ast').

This means that the model is hallucinating a function that is not even implemented.
I found that some users already experienced this same behaviour (https://community.openai.com/t/function-calling-a-python-function-is-frequently-called-even-though-it-does-not-exist-in-the-functions-parameter/264481).


I could fix this behaviour through some prompt engineering in the Pandas Agent Prefix + a modification to the python_repl_ast tool name (from my tests, it appears that everytime 'python' is present the tool name the model invokes the non-existent 'python' tool).

By the way, the changes proposed under the openai_functions_agent would be reverted, as well as the new regex on the sanitization function. These were just fixing a problem that didnt quite reside there.

In conclusion, i'd be happy to push my final changes of the solution i described, but i'd like to know beforehand how reluctant to changing the repl tool's name are you, since my solution depends on it.

Cheers!

Because renaming the AST tool is unlikely, I'll close this PR for now, and let me know if you'd like it reopened!

```

This enables me to write tests exercising code that handles function responses.

author: nfcampos

body:
@nfcampos if you really want to do that, then we need to make some decisions about how. I've spent a LOT of time on this PR, and I don't want to do any more work unless I have a clear picture of what is needed to get this committed.

The entire purpose of having the two different types (lists, and lists of lists), is to support multiple responses for both streaming chunks and non-streaming full responses.

In a testing environment, it doesn't really make sense to test non-streaming with lists of lists, and streaming with lists. But if you really want to support all types for both streaming and non-streaming, then we need to decide how we'd transform lists of lists if they were used for non-streaming, and lists if they were used for streaming.

I would propose this:

* For non-streaming requests, if a response is a list of lists, then the inner list would have all elements concatenated into a single response string.
* For streaming requests, if a response is a list, then each list element would be wrapped inside a list.

This would enabled a regular list to be passed for streaming, and it would stream only a single chunk for that response, and for non-streaming, all chunks would be put together into a single response.

Will this approach be sufficient to meet your requirements?
author: thehunmonkgroup

body:
> changing param names is a breaking change, im not sure it's justified here — could we just clarify the docstring?

Target modules run inference based on SentenceTransformer module. In the original code, param : model_name passed to the self.client, which is a SentenceTransformer instance. It is the only usage of the 'model_name' param. 

However, below is the annotation for the 'model_name_and_path' param of  SentenceTransformer module, in which the 'model_name' param of our original code putted. 
":param model_name_or_path: If it is a filepath on disc, it loads the model from that path. If it is not a path, it first tries to download a pre-trained SentenceTransformer model. If that fails, tries to construct a model from Huggingface models repository with that name."
Here is the permalink. https://github.com/UKPLab/sentence-transformers/blob/a458ce79c40fef93d5ecc66931b446ea65fdd017/sentence_transformers/SentenceTransformer.py#L37

'model_name_and_path' is way more natural.
author: sangwongenip

body:
> changing param names is a breaking change, im not sure it's justified here — could we just clarify the docstring?

If there is any problem, please let me know :)
author: sangwongenip

body:
Hey @sangwongenip ! Closing this for the reason @baskaryan outlined above. This change will break any users who have something like `HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name=...)` in their code, and while I agree the new name is clearer, that clarity is not worth breaking the code of anyone using it like this.

If you're interested in helping out with this, I would recommend a followup PR clarifying that a path can be passed (and how to format it) in the docstring, or adding it to the docs :)

body: Why isn't the sandbox enabled by default, but instead there is a warning about risks in jinja2?
author: everyun

body:
By the way that jinja2 is designed, it is not possible to create a sandbox from _inside_ a running Python process. It is not something the `langchain` library can provide or enable. The sandbox has to be set up externally, around the entire app that the end user is running. For example, this could be done via virtualization.

Of course, it's best to completely avoid jinja2 if possible, because of the difficulty in setting up such a sandbox properly.
author: obi1kenobi

body: is `sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment().from_string(f).render` not safe enough? why we need an external sandbox?
author: everyun

body:
It's very nice and we're looking into adopting it, but it unfortunately isn't safe enough to justify _not_ recommending an external sandbox. One of the concerns is that the jinja sandbox security model is "assume safe unless marked" instead of "assume unsafe unless marked." It relies on functions being explicitly marked as [unsafe](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.1.x/sandbox/#jinja2.sandbox.unsafe), which is very difficult to do safely in a large fast-moving project like this one. All it would take is one slip-up and attackers would have a way in.

Here I'm explicitly _not_ saying that jinja made a poor design decision. That design is very reasonable from an adoption and ease of use perspective — the safer alternative would probably be quite onerous to use. All I'm saying is that its security model isn't quite a match for our needs and concerns :)

body:
> @baskaryan how do you mean? the other subclasses don't have additional args?

```python
class HumanMessage(BaseMessage):
    """A Message from a human."""

    example: bool = False
    """Whether this Message is being passed in to the model as part of an example 
        conversation.
    """

    @property
    def type(self) -> str:
        """Type of the message, used for serialization."""
        return "human"


class HumanMessageChunk(HumanMessage, BaseMessageChunk):
    """A Human Message chunk."""

    pass
```

some messages have `example`, FunctionMessage has `name`. for human/ai msg probs doesn't matter bc generated stuff won't be examples (and won't be human msg) but Functions name could matter? and more generally if we add any other params to subclasses in future it's not obv with this method being inherited that something would need to be updated

body: @jaikanthjay46 This makes it work for ChatGenerations to? Is there a reason that JSON didn't. @baskaryan and I talked about this but I can't remember why. whats the underlying serialization now?
author: Spartee

body:
> @jaikanthjay46 This makes it work for ChatGenerations to? Is there a reason that JSON didn't. @baskaryan and I talked about this but I can't remember why. whats the underlying serialization now? 

It is serialised to JSON, since we use langchain's `loads` and `dumps` it stores it with Langchain Object metadata and reconstructs the objects automatically for `Generation`, `ChatGeneration` and beyond.

I have a variation of this I use for work, which uses just plain old `json.dumps` and `_message_to_dict` from messages.py, but have 2 different serialisation functions, one for `Generation` and other for `ChatGeneration` and depending on the contents deserialise them into the same. It uses less memory but would need maintain it when introducing a `NewGeneration`

body: Great addition, @annjawn. I just made an update for DocumentIntelligence which also rolls up paragraphs that are under the same SectionHeading to generate larger documents that are semantically similar per structure of the document. Also from previous experiments it seems that tables and paragraphs from the DI API overlap, so I used the spans to come up with an ordered list of non-overlapping text chunks. Would you mind having a look at https://github.com/LarsAC/langchain/tree/larsac/azure-di?
author: LarsAC

body:
Hey @LarsAC , yes technically LINES/WORDS/PARAGRAPHS will indeed overlap with TABLE. The idea for including TABLE is to provide a way for people to use that in Self-query. However, we may still want to include it in the text as well (it's probably a matter of just looking at `type` = `PAGE` | `PARAGRAPH` if the user is interested in plain text only, or `type` = `TABLE_HEADER` & `TABLE_ROW` if user is interested in the Tables. I also just added PAGE level and PARAGRAPH level chunking based on which the user prefers using `split_mode`. 

I will definitely take a look at your updates 👍, though I am thinking if we should still provide some flexibility of how the user may want to retrieve the text from the doc.
author: annjawn

body: @annjawn Fully agree with the flexibility. I had also added a "switch" parameter to the constructor of the loader in order to let the user control how to parse the text. We could likely add more options in parallel.

Edit: I went ahead and readded backwards compatibility with `GoogleCloudEnterpriseSearchRetriever`. I found another way to do it that made the code less complicated, and will make it seamless/less confusing for existing users.

~Yes, I did originally. You can see in the commit history. However, this was confusing users that were trying to use my forked version specifically because of the parameter name changes. (Search Engines and Data Stores used to share the same ID in previous versions of the product, but now they don't, and it was too confusing to have both parameters be available).~

~This is supposed to be a net new thing, with a redirect from the old docs page to the new one.~

~Anyone that doesn't want to change to the new version can stay on an older version of LangChain. (It's a very straightforward change to make, I can even add a more explicit migration guide in the docs, but I already have sections that discuss the previous versions)~

body:
I will start working on adding Exllamav2 to langchain
Meanwhile, here is a complete script that will let you use the ExllamaV1 with langchain written by @EkChinHui & adapted by me
almost all GPTQ models work with that, except some latest models that have a wider vocab like 'CapybaraHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B-GPTQ' which raises an 'IndexError: Out of range: piece id is out of range'. I will handle that in the v2 script.

```py
import glob
import os
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional

from langchain.callbacks.manager import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
from langchain.chains import LLMChain
from langchain.llms.base import LLM
from langchain.schema.output import GenerationChunk
from langchain_core.callbacks import StreamingStdOutCallbackHandler
from langchain_core.prompts import PromptTemplate
from pydantic.v1 import Field, root_validator


class Exllama(LLM):
    """Exllama API.

    To use, you should have the exllama library installed, and provide the
    path to the Llama model as a named parameter to the constructor.
    Check out: https://github.com/jllllll/exllama

    Example:
        .. code-block:: python

        from langchain.llms import Exllama
        llm = Exllama(model_path="/path/to/llama/model")
    """

    client: Any  #: :meta private:
    model_path: str
    """The path to the GPTQ model folder."""
    exllama_cache: Any = None  #: :meta private:
    config: Any = None  #: :meta private:
    generator: Any = None  #: :meta private:
    tokenizer: Any = None  #: :meta private:

    # Langchain parameters
    logfunc = print
    stop_sequences: List[str] = Field("")
    """Sequences that immediately will stop the generator."""

    streaming: Optional[bool] = Field(True)
    """Whether to stream the results, token by token."""

    # Generator parameters
    disallowed_tokens: Optional[List[int]] = Field(None)
    """List of tokens to disallow during generation."""

    temperature: Optional[float] = Field(None)
    """Temperature for sampling diversity."""

    top_k: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    """Consider the most probable top_k samples, 0 to disable top_k sampling."""

    top_p: Optional[float] = Field(None)
    """Consider tokens up to a cumulative probabiltiy of top_p,
    0.0 to disable top_p sampling."""

    min_p: Optional[float] = Field(None)
    """Do not consider tokens with probability less than this."""

    typical: Optional[float] = Field(None)
    """Locally typical sampling threshold, 0.0 to disable typical sampling."""

    token_repetition_penalty_max: Optional[float] = Field(None)
    """Repetition penalty for most recent tokens."""

    token_repetition_penalty_sustain: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    """No. most recent tokens to repeat penalty for, -1 to apply to whole context."""

    token_repetition_penalty_decay: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    """Gradually decrease penalty over this many tokens."""

    beams: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    """Number of beams for beam search."""

    beam_length: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    """Length of beams for beam search."""

    # Config overrides
    max_seq_len: int = Field(2048)
    """Reduce to save memory. Can also be increased,
    ideally while also using compress_pos_emn and a compatible model/LoRA"""

    compress_pos_emb: Optional[float] = Field(1.0)
    """Amount of compression to apply to the positional embedding."""

    set_auto_map: Optional[str] = Field(None)
    """Comma-separated list of VRAM (in GB) to use per GPU device for model layers,
    e.g. 20,7,7"""

    gpu_peer_fix: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    """Prevent direct copies of data between GPUs"""

    alpha_value: Optional[float] = Field(1.0)
    """Rope context extension alpha"""

    # Tuning
    matmul_recons_thd: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    fused_mlp_thd: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    sdp_thd: Optional[int] = Field(None)
    fused_attn: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    matmul_fused_remap: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    rmsnorm_no_half2: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    rope_no_half2: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    matmul_no_half2: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    silu_no_half2: Optional[bool] = Field(None)
    concurrent_streams: Optional[bool] = Field(None)

    # Lora Parameters
    lora_path: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Path to your lora.")

    @staticmethod
    def get_model_path_at(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
        patterns = ["*.safetensors", "*.bin", "*.pt"]
        model_paths = []
        for pattern in patterns:
            full_pattern = os.path.join(path, pattern)
            model_paths = glob.glob(full_pattern)
            if model_paths:  # If there are any files matching the current pattern
                break  # Exit the loop as soon as we find a matching file
        if model_paths:  # If there are any files matching any of the patterns
            return model_paths[0]
        else:
            return None  # Return None if no matching files were found

    @staticmethod
    def configure_object(
        params: List[str], values: Dict[str, Any], logfunc: Callable[[str], None]
    ) -> Callable[[str], None]:
        obj_params = {k: values.get(k) for k in params}

        def apply_to(obj: str) -> None:
            for key, value in obj_params.items():
                if value:
                    if hasattr(obj, key):
                        setattr(obj, key, value)
                        logfunc(f"{key} {value}")
                    else:
                        raise AttributeError(f"{key} does not exist in {obj}")

        return apply_to

    @root_validator()
    def validate_environment(cls, values: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        try:
            from exllama.generator import ExLlamaGenerator
            from exllama.lora import ExLlamaLora
            from exllama.model import ExLlama, ExLlamaCache, ExLlamaConfig
            from exllama.tokenizer import ExLlamaTokenizer
        except ImportError:
            raise ImportError(
                "Could not import exllama library. "
                "Please install the exllama library with (cuda 11.8 is required)"
                "!python -m pip install git+https://github.com/jllllll/exllama"
            )
        model_path = values["model_path"]
        lora_path = values["lora_path"]

        tokenizer_path = os.path.join(model_path, "tokenizer.model")
        model_config_path = os.path.join(model_path, "config.json")
        model_path = Exllama.get_model_path_at(model_path)

        config = ExLlamaConfig(model_config_path)
        tokenizer = ExLlamaTokenizer(tokenizer_path)
        config.model_path = model_path

        # Set logging function if verbose or set to empty lambda
        verbose = values["verbose"]
        if not verbose:
            values["logfunc"] = lambda *args, **kwargs: None
        logfunc = values["logfunc"]

        model_param_names = [
            "temperature",
            "top_k",
            "top_p",
            "min_p",
            "typical",
            "token_repetition_penalty_max",
            "token_repetition_penalty_sustain",
            "token_repetition_penalty_decay",
            "beams",
            "beam_length",
        ]

        config_param_names = [
            "max_seq_len",
            "compress_pos_emb",
            "gpu_peer_fix",
            "alpha_value",
        ]

        tuning_parameters = [
            "matmul_recons_thd",
            "fused_mlp_thd",
            "sdp_thd",
            "matmul_fused_remap",
            "rmsnorm_no_half2",
            "rope_no_half2",
            "matmul_no_half2",
            "silu_no_half2",
            "concurrent_streams",
            "fused_attn",
        ]

        configure_config = Exllama.configure_object(config_param_names, values, logfunc)
        configure_config(config)
        configure_tuning = Exllama.configure_object(tuning_parameters, values, logfunc)
        configure_tuning(config)
        configure_model = Exllama.configure_object(model_param_names, values, logfunc)

        # Special parameter, set auto map, it's a function
        if values["set_auto_map"]:
            config.set_auto_map(values["set_auto_map"])
            logfunc(f"set_auto_map {values['set_auto_map']}")

        model = ExLlama(config)
        exllama_cache = ExLlamaCache(model)
        generator = ExLlamaGenerator(model, tokenizer, exllama_cache)

        # Load and apply lora to generator
        if lora_path is not None:
            lora_config_path = os.path.join(lora_path, "adapter_config.json")
            lora_path = Exllama.get_model_path_at(lora_path)
            lora = ExLlamaLora(model, lora_config_path, lora_path)
            generator.lora = lora
            logfunc(f"Loaded LORA @ {lora_path}")

        # Configure the model and generator
        values["stop_sequences"] = [x.strip().lower() for x in values["stop_sequences"]]

        configure_model(generator.settings)
        setattr(generator.settings, "stop_sequences", values["stop_sequences"])
        logfunc(f"stop_sequences {values['stop_sequences']}")

        disallowed = values.get("disallowed_tokens")
        if disallowed:
            generator.disallow_tokens(disallowed)
            print(f"Disallowed Tokens: {generator.disallowed_tokens}")

        values["client"] = model
        values["generator"] = generator
        values["config"] = config
        values["tokenizer"] = tokenizer
        values["exllama_cache"] = exllama_cache

        return values

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        """Return type of llm."""
        return "Exllama"

    def get_num_tokens(self, text: str) -> int:
        """Get the number of tokens present in the text."""
        return self.generator.tokenizer.num_tokens(text)

    def _call(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        stop: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        run_manager: Optional[CallbackManagerForLLMRun] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> str:
        combined_text_output = ""
        for chunk in self._stream(prompt=prompt, stop=stop, run_manager=run_manager):
            combined_text_output += chunk.text
        return combined_text_output

    from enum import Enum

    class MatchStatus(Enum):
        EXACT_MATCH = 1
        PARTIAL_MATCH = 0
        NO_MATCH = 2

    def match_status(self, sequence: str, banned_sequences: List[str]) -> MatchStatus:
        sequence = sequence.strip().lower()
        for banned_seq in banned_sequences:
            if banned_seq == sequence:
                return self.MatchStatus.EXACT_MATCH
            elif banned_seq.startswith(sequence):
                return self.MatchStatus.PARTIAL_MATCH
        return self.MatchStatus.NO_MATCH

    def _stream(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        stop: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        run_manager: Optional[CallbackManagerForLLMRun] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Iterator[GenerationChunk]:
        # config = self.config
        generator = self.generator
        beam_search = (
            self.beams
            and self.beams >= 1
            and self.beam_length
            and self.beam_length >= 1
        )

        ids = generator.tokenizer.encode(prompt)
        generator.gen_begin_reuse(ids)

        if beam_search:
            generator.begin_beam_search()
            token_getter = generator.beam_search
        else:
            generator.end_beam_search()
            token_getter = generator.gen_single_token

        last_newline_pos = 0
        match_buffer = ""

        seq_length = len(generator.tokenizer.decode(generator.sequence_actual[0]))
        response_start = seq_length
        cursor_head = response_start

        while generator.gen_num_tokens() <= (
            self.max_seq_len - 4
        ):  # Slight extra padding space as we seem to occasionally get a
            # few more than 1-2 tokens
            # Fetch a token
            token = token_getter()

            # If it's the ending token replace it and end the generation.
            if token.item() == generator.tokenizer.eos_token_id:
                generator.replace_last_token(generator.tokenizer.newline_token_id)
                if beam_search:
                    generator.end_beam_search()
                return

            # Tokenize the string from the last new line, we can't just decode the
            # last token due to how sentencepiece decodes.
            stuff = generator.tokenizer.decode(
                generator.sequence_actual[0][last_newline_pos:]
            )
            cursor_tail = len(stuff)
            chunk = stuff[cursor_head:cursor_tail]
            cursor_head = cursor_tail

            # Append the generated chunk to our stream buffer
            match_buffer = match_buffer + chunk

            if token.item() == generator.tokenizer.newline_token_id:
                last_newline_pos = len(generator.sequence_actual[0])
                cursor_head = 0
                cursor_tail = 0

            # Check if the stream buffer is one of the stop sequences
            status = self.match_status(match_buffer, self.stop_sequences)

            if status == self.MatchStatus.EXACT_MATCH:
                # Encountered a stop, rewind generator to before we hit the match stop.
                rewind_length = generator.tokenizer.encode(match_buffer).shape[-1]
                generator.gen_rewind(rewind_length)
                if beam_search:
                    generator.end_beam_search()
                return
            elif status == self.MatchStatus.PARTIAL_MATCH:
                # Partially matched a stop, continue buffering but don't yield.
                continue
            elif status == self.MatchStatus.NO_MATCH:
                if run_manager:
                    run_manager.on_llm_new_token(
                        token=match_buffer,
                        verbose=self.verbose,
                    )

                # yield match_buffer  # Not a stop, yield the match buffer.
                # match_buffer = ""
                chunk = GenerationChunk(text=match_buffer)
                yield chunk  # Not a stop, yield the match buffer.

                match_buffer = ""
        return


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Callbacks support token-wise streaming
    callbacks = [StreamingStdOutCallbackHandler()]

    template = """Question: {question}

    Answer: Let's think step by step."""

    prompt = PromptTemplate(template=template, input_variables=["question"])

    # Verbose is required to pass to the callback manager
    llm = Exllama(
        model_path="models/TheBloke_Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GPTQ",
        callbacks=callbacks,
        verbose=True,
    )
    llm_chain = LLMChain(prompt=prompt, llm=llm)

    question = "What NFL team won the Super Bowl in the year Justin Bieber was born?"

    llm_chain.invoke({"question": question})

 ```

body: worth noting changing init signature and serdes logic are both breaking changes so we should be sure they're worth making
author: baskaryan

body:
I agree, which is why I had thought a bit about this before making these choices. Here's my reasoning on these two points:

1. Serdes. Since these classes are used for caching, missing items pre-post-migration is supposedly not a dramatic thing, compared to the extended support for Chat* storage one gains. I could add logic to catch the json exception and silently return a cache miss (just a warning, no error) in case an "old format" entry is encountered, that would probably be a net gain. Given the "disposable" nature of cache items, I thought adding a legacy-compatibility layer would have been more a burden than an advantage.
2. The init signature. This is more speculative, but one thing that is in the making on the CassIO side is another connection method `cassio.init(...)`, followed by lightweight init of possibly several classes leaving session/keyspace unspecified (i.e. default). As a named-parameter paradigm is anyway very common in all things around LLM/GenAI tooling in my experience (with everything evolving so fast!) I took the plunge and thought "better now than later". But on this point I am slightly less certain than on the previous.

In any case, I am deeply grateful for the extremely fast reaction to this PR :)

author: baskaryan

body:
Thank you for sharing your thoughts. I agree with both points. Here's an update where:
1. errors from malformed cache entries are handled softly with a warning, no exceptions, just yet another cache miss;
2. while I was at it, compatibility with the legacy format for cached entries is recovered (a warning is logged)
3. restored the init method in the semantic cache somewhat: kept the parameter order unchanged, just made session/keyspace Optional as you suggest. Once the `init()` method of cassIO is fleshed out fully and makes it to PyPI, this might be revised, but it's fine for me not to anticipate it here.

Cheers!

body: hm not super familiar with what kwargs should be passed in during pipeline instantiation vs at inference time, is there an argument that we should have a separate inference_kwargs param to handle your example?
author: baskaryan

body:
> hm not super familiar with what kwargs should be passed in during pipeline instantiation vs at inference time, is there an argument that we should have a separate inference_kwargs param to handle your example?

All arguments for hf_pipeline inference can be supplied at instantiation and stored into [`self._forward_params`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/0a55d9f7376f72ad3ff296d4249840021b03bcc4/src/transformers/pipelines/base.py#L830C44-L830C44), but the reverse is not true, there are some arguments at instantiation that can't be passed at inference. Most of the such arguments aren't relevant (like `image_processor` or `feature_extractor`, which are only used for images), and I am not sure how relevant are the rest, like `framework` (i.e. torch vs tf), `modelcard`, `revision` [etc](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/0a55d9f7376f72ad3ff296d4249840021b03bcc4/src/transformers/pipelines/base.py#L762-L773). 
The only argument that is definitely useful is `torch_dtype`, which is currently being passed through `pipeline_kwargs`, but with this fix it will break inference if instantiated with `HuggingFacePipeline.from_model_id`. 
Would it make more sense to make `torch_dtype` a separate argument for `.from_model_id` instead of making an entire dictionary?
author: sergey-volokhin

body:
Actually, in the current version the fix breaks if instantiating the pipeline using `__init__`, because `self.pipeline_kwargs` and `self.model_kwargs` are `None`, instead of `{}`, like when instantiating using `.from_model_id` ([here](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/116cc7998cac563894bdf0037259db767882b55c/libs/langchain/langchain/llms/huggingface_pipeline.py#L125) and [here](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/116cc7998cac563894bdf0037259db767882b55c/libs/langchain/langchain/llms/huggingface_pipeline.py#L86)):

I think that the default values of [`model_kwargs`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/116cc7998cac563894bdf0037259db767882b55c/libs/langchain/langchain/llms/huggingface_pipeline.py#L51C40-L51C40) and [`pipeline_kwargs`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/116cc7998cac563894bdf0037259db767882b55c/libs/langchain/langchain/llms/huggingface_pipeline.py#L53) should be changed to `{}` to maintain the parity:

```python
# code from the `.from_model_id` example in the documentation
from langchain.llms import HuggingFacePipeline 
hf = HuggingFacePipeline.from_model_id(
    model_id="gpt2",
    task="text-generation",
    pipeline_kwargs={"max_new_tokens": 10},
)
```
```
hf.model_kwargs == {}
hf.pipeline_kwargs == {"max_new_tokens": 10}
```
and
``` python
# code from the direct passing example in the documentation
from langchain.llms import HuggingFacePipeline
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline

model_id = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)
pipe = pipeline(
    "text-generation", model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, max_new_tokens=10
)
hf = HuggingFacePipeline(pipeline=pipe)
```
```
hf.model_kwargs is None
hf.pipeline_kwargs is None
```

body:
The issue is solved in this [commit](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/commit/641efcf41c8358655dcf1db2fbe827cfe77feae0) by @baskaryan. 

The only potential concern is that parity is still broken:
```python
from transformers import pipeline
from langchain import HuggingFacePipeline

hf = HuggingFacePipeline.from_model_id(
    model_id="gpt2",
    task="text-generation",
)
hf.pipeline_kwargs == {}, hf.model_kwargs == {}

# but 

hf = HuggingFacePipeline(pipeline=pipeline('text-generation', model='gpt2'))
hf.pipeline_kwargs is None, hf.model_kwargs is None
```

but it doesn't seem to matter too much at the moment, so this issue can be closed.
Thank you.

Hi @baskaryan and @hwchase17 ,
I saw that the structure code was updated and the **delete** feature was implemented.
We have a problem: If the developers used the old version, they can't know what the primary key field (id) was
So I have updated a new feature: get_ids. That helps us easily get the primary key by expression
Meanwhile, I also added the **upsert** feature to insert or update documents
Thanks

body:
Strange. I have been testing with pydantic 1 and 2. I haven't seen that error, but I've got the message above about an encode method. I've tried poking around a bit to see where that comes from, and here's something strange: it seems like it only happens when the api key is passed as a keyword argument. If it's pulled from environment variables, then it works as expected (in my case). Aside from that, I'm still trying to find the source of the error. 

Edit / note: maybe it has something to do with serialization and kwargs

```python
from langchain.chat_models import ChatAnthropic

llm_with_kwargs = ChatAnthropic(
	anthropic_api_key="..."
)
print(llm_with_kwargs.predict("hello"))

# ... AttributeError: 'SecretStr' object has no attribute 'encode'

llm_with_kwargs._lc_kwargs

# {'anthropic_api_key': '...'}


import os
os.environ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'] = "..."

llm_with_env = ChatAnthropic()
print(llm_with_env.predict("hello"))

#  Hello! My name is Claude.

llm_with_env._lc_kwargs

# {}
```

I think it's essential that the api keys are kept private, but since I certainly did not observe any of this behavior before submitting this PR, I'd be in favor of rolling back the change.

body:
```
    @root_validator()
    def validate_environment(cls, values: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Validate that api key and python package exists in environment."""
        values["anthropic_api_key"] = SecretStr(
            get_from_dict_or_env(values, "anthropic_api_key", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        )
```

The problem with the "incorrect type" error is occurring here (llms/anthropic.py, line 64).  The anthropic_api_key value in values is already of type SecretStr, so the attempt to make it a SecretStr causes a type exception.   It appears that Pydantic internally coerces the str to a SecretStr; perhaps during individual field validation?  I don't know enough about Pydantic to be confident in providing a patch, but I can say that a conditional assignment such as the following resolves the bug:

```
    @root_validator()
    def validate_environment(cls, values: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Validate that api key and python package exists in environment."""
        raw_anthropic_api_key = get_from_dict_or_env(values, "anthropic_api_key", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        anthropic_api_key = raw_anthropic_api_key if isinstance(raw_anthropic_api_key, SecretStr) else SecretStr(raw_anthropic_api_key)
        values["anthropic_api_key"] = anthropic_api_key
```

body:
Hi, @eyurtsev , overall it looks great! Thanks for adding more tests!

I'm a bit puzzled about one aspect and hoped you could help me understand better. Towards the end, are we using the regular `load` and `lazy_load` methods in `BaseLoader` and then converting them to an async iterator shortly after?

If that’s the case, there might be a tiny hitch – the original iterator being synchronous could mean that fetching the next item might still block the event loop, even though the wrapper is asynchronous. Would love your thoughts on this! 🤔

Besides that, I think https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/10726#discussion_r1337274418 subclassing could be a good approach to handle different interfaces and avoid runtime errors and unexpected outcomes when dealing with async on applications endpoints. Would love to hear more of it!
author: jvelezmagic

body:
@jvelezmagic I was thinking to accept a BaseLoader and eventually use an async implementation when it's available, but fall back on the sync for now. A user can leverage the async features by passing an async iterator directly (not a BaseLoader). If this is confusing, we could limit the async version of the API to accept either an async iterator or sync iterator, but not BaseLoader for the time being. 

If user provides:
- async iterator they will benefit from async related speed ups, 
- sync iterator, it works but potentially with blocking calls (but user is aware of what they feed into the API),
- BaseLoader raises NotImplementedError until async api is added
 
We definitely want to add support for async on the loaders as well, but it's touching the base schema so it's too big of a change for this PR.

For example, when building a personalized assistant, the assistant might want to remember the user's preferences.

If user specifies a suffix,  it'll be better to leave the choice to the user to decide whether to include df_head in prompt. which can actually be inferred from the suffix prompt.

In the current implementation, the user prompt without a {df_head}  will raise an unexpected error, (because you cannot set it to false).   Therefore, I draft this PR to solve this problem.


maybe in line 76,  `_get_single_prompt` function
```
    if suffix is not None:
        suffix_to_use = suffix
        include_df_head = True
```
should be changed to 

   ```
 if suffix is not None:
        suffix_to_use = suffix
        include_df_head = include_df_in_prompt

```

body:
# PR #10866 Review: beef up agent docs

**Repository:** langchain-ai/langchain | **Author:** hwchase17 | **Files Changed:** 28 (+1964/-619)

---

## Overview

This PR restructures and significantly enhances the agent documentation. Key themes: documentation consolidation, LCEL-first approach in new notebooks, API reference expansion, and content relocation.

---

## File-by-File Review

### 1. `create_api_rst.py` (Modified, +4/-1)
Adds `agents.output_parsers` and `agents.format_scratchpad` to top-level API reference.
**Suggestion:** Wrap hard-coded submodule access in try/except to avoid silent KeyError.

### 2. `agent_types/index.mdx` (Modified, +7/-12)
Heading promotion ### to ##, plan-and-execute section removed.
**Suggestion:** Verify all `.html` links resolve correctly after restructuring.

### 3. `agents/index.mdx` (Modified, +27/-10)
New terminology section (AgentAction, AgentFinish, intermediate_steps), rewritten Agent section, Next Steps section.
**Suggestion:** Link type definitions to API reference. Add error handling note to AgentExecutor pseudocode.

### 4. `chat_conversation_agent.ipynb` (Added, +528)
Three-tier structure: LCEL, off-the-shelf, chat model.
**CRITICAL:** Cell 27 uses undefined `OPENAI_API_KEY` variable - will raise NameError. Fix: remove the param or define it from env.
**Also:** Cell 15 (off-the-shelf) has no output.

### 5. `openai_functions_agent.ipynb` (Added, +259)
LCEL-based function-calling agent construction.
**CRITICAL:** Hardcoded path `sqlite:///../../../../../notebooks/Chinook.db` not portable.
**Also:** Cells 13-14 not executed. Unused `OpenAI` import.

### 6. `openai_multi_functions_agent.ipynb` (Modified, +3/-3)
Added max_iterations demo.
**Suggestion:** Note the switch from MULTI_FUNCTIONS to OPENAI_FUNCTIONS between cells.

### 7. `react.ipynb` (Added, +365)
Most polished notebook. Four variants with consistent query.
**Issues:** Cells 22/24 not executed. Typo: steet should be steer (Cell 16). Deprecated .run() in Cell 24.

### 8. `self_ask_with_search.ipynb` (Modified, +147/-21)
LCEL section is excellent. Clear pipe operator chain.

### 9. `structured_chat.ipynb` (Added, +294)
Async execution with Playwright toolkit.
**Issue:** stop=[Observation] inconsistent with stop=[
Observation] in other notebooks. Empty Cell 16.

### 10. `plan_and_execute.mdx` (Renamed, +8/-0)
Good relocation to autonomous agents section. Full content inlined.

### 11-12. Deleted Files (6 files)
Skeleton pages and snippet files properly removed. Content relocated to notebooks and index pages.

---

## Recurring Issues

| Issue | Severity |
|-------|----------|
| Undefined OPENAI_API_KEY | HIGH |
| Unexecuted cells | MEDIUM |
| Hardcoded Chinook.db path | MEDIUM |
| Missing pip install | MEDIUM |
| Stop sequence inconsistency | LOW |
| Typo, deprecated API | LOW |

---

## Overall Assessment

**Strengths:** Three-tier pedagogical structure (LCEL, off-the-shelf, chat model) is excellent. LCEL demos demystify initialize_agent. API reference expansion improves discoverability.

**Verdict:** High-value docs PR. The OPENAI_API_KEY NameError in chat_conversation_agent Cell 27 is the only critical bug. All other issues are minor and easily fixable.

body:
No problem. Besides that, I've noticed that the split function interprets the inputs as regex expressions, which can sometimes lead to unexpected behaviour. 

For instance: the LLM implementation can pass `stop` parameters to the appropriate model (or inference API) and then it will call the `enforce_stop_tokens` function to be 100% sure that there is no extra text after the stop sequence has been reached.

So where is the problem?
If you pass `stop=["."]`, the API will interpret the stop sequences as is, but the helper function interprets the `.` as regex matching any character yielding in an empty result.

My solution to that problem was to make a slight modification to the function: https://github.com/IBM/ibm-generative-ai/blob/a83bd17db819a69f4891471448c5a4da52245d6c/src/genai/extensions/langchain/llm.py#L194C5-L194C5

Nice one @aHardReset! A couple things I noticed:
- Removing `filter` from those methods would be a breaking change for anyone using them. Do we have a strategy around breaking changes @baskaryan?
- `postgrest_filter` (with the `t`) wasn't a typo - it refers to filters passed to the [PostgREST API](https://postgrest.org/en/stable/references/api/tables_views.html) which Supabase uses to interface with the database (and used by the [self-querying retriever](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/b4354b769442fb94a700abc02a18c2bffb1fa806/libs/langchain/langchain/retrievers/self_query/supabase.py))
- We should probably document this change

Otherwise LGTM, will be good to provide more flexibility to the vector store 👍

Have you tried swapping `Bedrock` LLM with `BedrockChat` and see if that fixes the issue? Also, we should make sure that this change does not break the `BedrockChat` class.

body:
@3coins 

I have and it does.

But, I'm not aware of the full scope of other implementations or classes that might use LLM in the background or more generally, that might not work with BedrockChat. Hence why I'm patching this instead of just recommending folks move to BedrockChat. But if someone could clarify that BedrockChat could encapsulate every implementation or use case, like for example, FewShotPrompts, I would recommend everyone migrate to BedrockChat and just ditch the LLM implementation.

The change does not break BedrockChat as per my testing. There are no unit or integrations tests that I could find though so this testing was very manual and limited.

body:
> @jonathancaevans The reason I am pushing `BedrockChat` is because it wraps the messages correctly (using LangChain Human/Assistant tags). Given that Anthropic LLM has deprecation warnings in their LLM and asking users to move the `ChatAnthropic` LLM, should we have the right guidance in the `Bedrock` LLM as well.
> 
> I also noticed that `Anthropic` LLM has similar code to wrap prompts in their LLM, but this was added a while ago (7 months). Given the urgency of this issue, I think it is fair to add the patch here at this time, as it is unlikely most folks will be able to migrate to the chat model class immediately.

seconding this. think the correct way to use bedrock and anthropic is via ChatModel interface (meaning BedrockChat). we should still fix the issues here but we should also log a warning if folks use Bedrock LLM with provider="anthropic" recommending they switch to BedrockChat

body:
@jonathancaevans Just spoke with one of your co-workers -- we have been digging into this since Monday's "internal memo".

I think we have a solution which works, and up to langchain v0.0.303 it worked.
I was trying to figure out why it stopped in v0.0.304 and v0.0.305 and saw this push.

I think we need to undo this.

The prompt:

```
ANTHROPIC_PROMPT = """\n\nHuman:

Current conversation:
[HISTORY]
{history}
[/HISTORY]

{input}\n\nAssistant:"""
```

Is what's needed.

That seems to work for both Antrhopic's, and Bedrock's.

Along with 2 other changes -- Making sure any conversation summary does not use the words "Human" and "Assistant" -- note: you can lower case those:

1.) `memory = ConversationSummaryBufferMemory(llm=memory_summary_llm, max_token_limit=max_token_count, human_prefix="User", ai_prefix="AI")`

and

2.) ```
message = message.replace("Human", r"\human")
message = message.replace("Assistant", r"\assistant")
```

^ the second is needed to sanitize the user input, as any input that has `Human` and `Assistant` will break it.

body: can we improve the existing classes instead of adding new ones? if the underlying integration is fundamentally there's no reason to have redundant classes
author: baskaryan

body:
Sure. I've added some commits to this pull request, and here is the improvement:

I removed the exsiting implementations of `langchain.chat_models.ErnieBotChat` and `langchain.embeddings.ErnieEmbeddings`, and left deprecation notes in their documentation. The reasons behind this are:

1. The functionality of `langchain.chat_models.ErnieBotChat` and `langchain.embeddings.ErnieEmbeddings` is already covered by `langchain.chat_models.QianfanChatEndpoint` and `langchain.embeddings.QianfanEmbeddingEndpoint`. Since these APIs allow Qianfan platform users to call the ERNIE Bot LLM, I think the `QianfanChatEndpoint` and `QianfanEmbeddingEndpoint` are clearer in naming. So I removed the existing `ErnieBotChat` and `ErnieEmbeddings`.
2. The newly added chat and embeddings models, named `ChatERNIEBot` and `ERNIEBotEmbeddings`, are used to replace the removed `ErnieBotChat` and `ErnieEmbeddings`. The new integrations offer enhanced features and allow AI Studio users to use ERNIE Bot. Now `ChatERNIEBot` and `QianfanChatEndpoint` coexist in LangChain, one for Qianfan users and the other for AI Studio users. There is no overlap.

@axiangcoding Please also take a look at this PR and see if the modifications are appropriate. Thanks!

body:
> @Bobholamovic Glad to see this PR about ERNIE-Bot, I've done some similar change in this #10830. Maybe we could merge these two PR into one? Looking forward to your reply. @baskaryan

Yes, it would be nice if we can merge these two PRs, as we are doing similar jobs. Having said so, I've found the following differences between the two PRs. Please take a look:

1. In #10830 , a pair of Qianfan AK and SK are used for authentication, which makes `ErnieBot` and `ErnieBotChat` functionally the same as `QianfanLLMEndpoint` and `QianfanChatEndpoint`. This might introduce redundency in APIs.
2. In this PR, an additional retry policy is implemented for the LLM and chat bot integrations, which helps the program to recover from unexpected failures of HTTP requests.
3. Unit tests for function calling are missing from this PR.

body:
> I recommend adding unit tests or an notebook sample for function calling in this PR.

@NuODaniel  Thanks for your suggestion. I've included function calling tests in this PR. 

A new description of what's introduced in this PR is as follows:

* Add `langchain.llms.ErnieBot` for text completion.
* Enhance `langchain.chat_models.ErnieBotChat` and `langchain.embeddings.ErnieEmbeddings`. 
    * The new implementation introduces more advanced features, such as streaming, asynchronous generation, and function calling. 
    * The code is refactored to base on the official ERNIE Bot SDK, which provides additional safety and robustness.
    * The overlap between `langchain.chat_models.ErnieBotChat`/`langchain.embeddings.ErnieEmbeddings` and `langchain.chat_models.QianfanChatEndpoint`/`langchain.embeddings.QianfanEmbeddingEndpoint` is eliminated. `ErnieBotChat`/`ErnieEmbeddings` is now intended to be used by AI Studio users, while `QianfanChatEndpoint`/`QianfanEmbeddingEndpoint` is designed for Qianfan users.
    * The documentation is improved. More examples are added in notebooks, including the examples on the usage of the advanced features.

@baskaryan Please take a look.

> https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/cfa2203c626a2287d60c1febeb3e3a68b77acd77/libs/langchain/langchain/vectorstores/elasticsearch.py
> 
> Could you explain what is different?

@eyurtsev Thanks for your review. The overall idea of this PR is to integrate the vectorstore capabilities of Baidu Cloud's elasticsearch (hereinafter referred to as BES) into langchain. The differences between the original elasticsearch code and BES are as follows: 1. BES and the community's ES differ in terms of indexing, querying, and other semantics; 2. Compared to community's ES, BES supports multiple index types and similarity algorithms, and its query semantics are different from ES.

body:
Sorry for the slow reply @WessZumino @baskaryan 

I think this was created before #9136 was merged. \
@WessZumino have you tried since then?

Unless I am missing something here, the filters should not yield much benefit (there are not too many classes in the rdf and rdfs namespaces). Instead, they might lead to undesired side-effects in edge cases, e.g., the user not being able to ask for all instances of rdf:property anymore; and rdf and rdfs can and should be treated separately.

Checking the example provided in #8907, I did notice another issue in the SPARQL queries when retrieving OWL classes, though.
I feel like that one can be resolved in a more straightforward way by adapting the queries as such:

```
# NOTE: here, being a class is defined as having instances.
#   this may lead to false negatives, but avoids mistaking instances for classes
cls_query_rdf = prefixes["rdfs"] + (
    """SELECT DISTINCT ?cls ?com\n"""
    """WHERE { \n"""
    """    ?instance a ?cls .\n"""
    """    OPTIONAL { ?cls rdfs:comment ?com } . \n"""
    """    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?cls a rdf:Property } \n"""
    """}"""
)

cls_query_rdfs = prefixes["rdfs"] + (
    """SELECT DISTINCT ?cls ?com\n"""
    """WHERE { \n"""
    """    ?cls a rdfs:Class . \n"""
    """    OPTIONAL { ?cls rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
    """    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?cls a rdf:Property } \n"""
    """}"""
)

cls_query_owl = prefixes["rdfs"] + prefixes["owl"] + (
    """SELECT DISTINCT ?cls ?com\n"""
    """WHERE { \n"""
    """    ?cls a owl:Class . \n"""
    """    FILTER (isIRI(?cls)) . \n"""
    """    OPTIONAL { ?cls rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
    """    FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?cls a rdf:Property } \n"""
    """}"""
)

rel_query_rdf = prefixes["rdfs"] + (
    """SELECT DISTINCT ?rel ?com\n"""
    """WHERE { \n"""
    """    ?subj ?rel ?obj . \n"""
    """    OPTIONAL { ?rel rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
    """}"""
)

rel_query_rdfs = (
    prefixes["rdf"]
    + prefixes["rdfs"]
    + (
        """SELECT DISTINCT ?rel ?com\n"""
        """WHERE { \n"""
        """    ?rel a rdf:Property . \n"""
        """    OPTIONAL { ?rel rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
        """}"""
    )
)

op_query_owl = (
    prefixes["rdfs"]
    + prefixes["owl"]
    + (
        """SELECT DISTINCT ?op ?com\n"""
        """WHERE { \n"""
        """    ?op a owl:ObjectProperty . \n"""
        """    OPTIONAL { ?op rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
        """}"""
    )
)

dp_query_owl = (
    prefixes["rdfs"]
    + prefixes["owl"]
    + (
        """SELECT DISTINCT ?dp ?com\n"""
        """WHERE { \n"""
        """    ?dp a owl:DatatypeProperty . \n"""
        """    OPTIONAL { ?dp rdfs:comment ?com } \n"""
        """}"""
    )
)
```

Could you try this? And if it does not work, could you provide a minimal example of where the filters you added make a difference?

BTW, I totally agree that fitting a large schema into the context window of a smaller language model is a challenge - something like an additional step for filtering the schema for notions relevant to the query might be the way to go in such cases.

And I do like the idea of using the prefixes if this improves the query generation - adding that together with documentation in a separate PR would be cool! \
What I did not get is what the description `param source_file` in `_get_namespaces` is for, however. So this might need some cleaning up.

body:
> for backwards compatibility + optionality, updated to check if prefix is already in the key and only add if it isn't. what do we think?

@Spartee @baskaryan LGTM >> My only input is that the current implementation, and this adjustment, still don't provide flexibility to allow for users to define their own index prefix right? It uses `_redis_prefix()` to generate this everytime. This will eventually need to change, but just highlighting that for future improvements.
author: tylerhutcherson

body:
@tylerhutcherson 
The current implementation does provide users the ability to define their own index prefix. 
While creating the Redis vector store object, user can provide the `index_name` argument, (see [base.py#L251](https://github.com/a9raag/langchain/blob/059a0c54ab9350ce93871ddb727ebbd879630c43/libs/langchain/langchain/vectorstores/redis/base.py#L251)) which is then used to generate the prefix for the document. `_redis_prefix(self.index_name)`  (see [base.py#L684](https://github.com/a9raag/langchain/blob/059a0c54ab9350ce93871ddb727ebbd879630c43/libs/langchain/langchain/vectorstores/redis/base.py#L684))
For example, 
```py
vector_store = Redis(
        redis_url = "localhost:6379", 
        index_name = "custom_prefix", 
        embedding = embedding)
```
will generate documents with key prefix `doc:custom_prefix:1234`
author: a9raag
Spartee

body:
> @a9raag, what Tyler is talking about is the “doc:” portion. You’re code shows the custom index name.
> 
> Users may want the flexibility to have multiple indicies with different prefixes, yet similar keys. (Or some combination of this). The previous methodology seemed introduced as a convenience, but limited the functionality.
> 
> Maybe we add the ability to define prefix? Seems like it might be a footgun.

^^ exactly -- redis is meant to be multi-tenant by design. So requiring the key prefix with `doc:` up front is an anti-pattern for redis, and could cause collisions in the overall keyspace depending on the use case. This should be a configurable setting, but could come in a later revision for the sake of simplicity. happy to help :)

> Where do you see it formats with `AI`? Believe everything Anthropic uses the formatting function being edited here (which uses Assistant)

For Bedrock Anthropic, which doesn't inherit for Anthropic, the following example will produce `AI:`, even if you explicitly use an `Assistant` role in the chat prompt template. I had to use a custom placeholder template to convert messages to `Assistant:`.

```python
SYSTEM_PROMPT = "You are a friendly assistant. This is a conversation between a human and an assistant."
prompt_template = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
    [
        ChatMessage(
            role="Instructions",
            content=SYSTEM_PROMPT
        ),
        HistoryPlaceholderTemplate(variable_name="history"),
        HumanMessagePromptTemplate.from_template("{input}"),
        ChatMessage(role="Assistant", content=""),
    ]
)
llm = BedrockChat(model_id="")
memory = ConversationBufferWindowMemory(return_messages=True, k=2)
llm_chain = ConversationChain(
    llm=llm, prompt=prompt_template, memory=memory, verbose=True
)
``` 
See my [PR](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyter-ai/pull/401/files#diff-61b6ffc90741cf3d7ba3038ef6a0ea0d28645adf64ce247a4420f711048dde2d) here to fix this in Jupyter AI. Ideally, we will want the this function from Anthropic in BedrockChat, which formats the AI messages correctly.

> The setup errors out with the regular Bedrock LLM.


think this happens because of the mix of a ChatPromptTemplate with an LLM. if you use BedrockChat (which is probably the way claude should be used) it works, or using a PromptTemplate should work, too (see below). 
```python
def create_chain():
    prompt_template = PromptTemplate.from_template(
        SYSTEM_PROMPT + "\n\n{history}\n\n{input}"
    )
    llm = Bedrock(model_id="anthropic.claude-v1", client=aws_client)
    memory = ConversationBufferWindowMemory(k=2, ai_prefix="Assistant")
    llm_chain = ConversationChain(llm=llm, prompt=prompt_template, memory=memory, verbose=True)

    return llm_chain
```

We should update ChatPromptTemplate to make the AIMessage prefix configurable when a chat prompt is converted to a string, but that's probably a separate pr

body: @rohan-uiuc All LLMs are instances of runnables and expose a [with_retry method](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/ffe6a449e055d54c10c6a29ba98137ec95f531fa/libs/langchain/langchain/schema/runnable/base.py#L431-L431).  Would using that method work for your usecase?
author: eyurtsev

body:
@eyurtsev thanks for a quick reply. My use case is running autonomous agents and I usually run into RateLimitError. It will be helpful to add support for infinite retries with exponential backoff ONLY if the error is RateLimitError. We do have stop_after_attempt arg where we could add a large number, but  there must be other scenarios where users want a custom retry mechanism on specific exceptions so it might be useful to add another argument in [RunnableRetry](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/ffe6a449e055d54c10c6a29ba98137ec95f531fa/libs/langchain/langchain/schema/runnable/retry.py#L37)  which can be used to set `kwargs["stop"] = stop_never` or exposing the `retry_decorator` as an argument. 

 Please let me know if you think this will help or if there is a better way to handle this and I will be happy to update my PR.
author: rohan-uiuc

body:
Hi @rohan-uiuc

Try the following:

1) set max_retries to 0 on the llm, so there's no retrying logic on the llm itself
2) use the with_retry wrapper and set the number of attempts to some large integer (100_000) You may be able to pass math.inf, but depends on what tenacity allows (the function signature is for an int). The retry method accepts a list of exceptions that can be retried
author: eyurtsev

body:
@rohan-uiuc let me know if that works for your use case or if / why it fails for your use case. 

The considerations:

1)  we'd rather built in more functionality into RunnableRetrys so functionality can be rolled out to all LangChain objects at once rather than one particular LLM
2) we want to make sure that it's possible to trace all the retries for monitoring purposes

body:
Hi @rohan-uiuc,

The code is using pydantic to do validation and one of the segments seems to instantiate LLMPlanner which expectes an LLMChain.

```
      # PLANNER
        planner = load_chat_planner(self.llm, system_prompt=PLANNER_PROMPT)
```

The best solution is to re-write the corresponding code using LCEL (it's likely simpler than you expect).

The planner is just an llm chain followed by a parser: 

```
    def plan(self, inputs: dict, callbacks: Callbacks = None, **kwargs: Any) -> Plan:
        """Given input, decide what to do."""
        llm_response = self.llm_chain.run(**inputs, stop=self.stop, callbacks=callbacks)
        return self.output_parser.parse(llm_response)
```

The equivalent of that in LCEL is: https://python.langchain.com/docs/expression_language/cookbook/prompt_llm_parser#prompttemplate--llm--outputparser

provide the parser, llm and prompt you need and chain them:

![image](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/assets/3205522/236af73b-0cf3-4664-b1ad-54484cc6708b)

body:
Still needs:
- [x] better deprecation warning message that points users to the new code to use
- [x] conversion of internal write uses to the new functions
- [x] conversion of internal read uses to make them use the new code path instead of using top-level `langchain` import
  - There's an unfortunate Python quirk: the `__getattr__()` in `langchain/__init__.py` creates a _separate_ copy of the `verbose` and `debug` variables, so setting `langchain.verbose` with this PR _does not_ actually set `langchain.utils.globals._verbose`.
  - I implemented a workaround: the new explicit setter functions set both copies, and the explicit getters will read both copies and return whichever one was set. That way using the new getters and setters is backward-compatible, and uses of the old top-level `langchain` values will also be able to set the values and see any changes done to them via the new APIs as well.
  - Using the old `langchain` top-level values directly now triggers a warning with a concrete suggestion to use the corresponding explicit get/set functions. At some point in the future when users have migrated to using the new API, we can remove the top-level values entirely.

body: Hey @erlichsefi ! Was there a particular module/object you ran into this bug with? The reason I ask is because this function is used all over the place, and there are a few edge cases that could expect empty strings (or even `False`) to resolve falsy and search the env vars.
author: efriis

body:
Thank you for looking into this @efriis, I've encountered this bug when using this function externally (i.e., my own code that uses langchain) and thought to fix it at the source.

The main issue here is where you are passing False in `data[key]`, the if-condition will evaluate it as false, and instead of returning the value `false` it will fall back to the default value. 
Eyeballing the use cases for this function across the repo, it seems you are using it only with strings and not booleans, so I don't see anyway my change will cause regression.
author: erlichsefi

body:
Got it. Would recommend defining your own `get_from_dict_or_env` with the desired behavior then, as this change could have unintended impact for other langchain users (see below).

Due to the type definition of this function, the return type expected is a string, so `False` doesn't make a ton of sense to support here.

Regarding empty strings:

Main case I see is an app like the langsmith playground, where there's a web server that might take in `google_api_key=""` because the user inputted an empty string in the UI, which should then default to the stored `GOOGLE_API_KEY` environment variable.

Let me know if you have any questions!

body: Hey @austinmw ! I don't think we want to add the bedrock `chat_model` to the `llms` package like this. Could you use `from langchain.chat_models import BedrockChat` in your code as-is?
author: efriis

body:
Hi @efriis , I noticed that downstream libraries like NeMo guardrails use `get_type_to_cls_dict` in order to determine which class to call. So currently you can specify `engine: 'amazon_bedrock'`, but it's not possibly to specify to use the chat class:

https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails/blob/5f2541edb3e1115d48fc219e6e4d287d2d759ca1/nemoguardrails/llm/providers.py#L47
author: austinmw

body:
Got it. I think this is something that should be handled on the NeMo guardrails side instead to add the chat models. 

This dictionary ultimately maps names to `BaseLLM`, which `BedrockChat` does not subclass (that's a `BaseChatModel` instead)

However, the way NeMo uses the dictionary would be compatible with both because it requires entries to be `BaseLanguageModel`, which is the superclass of both `BaseLLM` and `BaseChatModel`.

If you need `BedrockChat` in your work, it looks like you can do something like the following in guardrails
```
from langchain.chat_models.bedrock import BedrockChat
from nemoguardrails.llm.providers import register_llm_provider
register_llm_provider('BedrockChat', BedrockChat)
```

Let me know if you have any other thoughts! Otherwise I'll close this
author: efriis

body:
> thanks for pr @ashleyxuu! what's the benefit of using this versus the VertexAI LLM directly?

BigFrames is a unified Python API on top of BigQuery’s managed storage and BigLake tables. BigFrames lets Python developers discover, describe, and understand the data available to them in BigQuery by providing a Python compatible API that can automatically scale to BigQuery sized datasets. VertexAI LLM is just the model.

So, BigFrames is a pivotal bridge connecting Google BigQuery with the diverse Python open source software ecosystem for data scientists. 

Our next goal is to support `_generate()` with DataFrame as input and output for large datasets. We can talk more about those use cases. My email is ashleyxu@google.com.

body: @ashleyxuu added a `generate_df` method that takes dataframes as input and returns dataframes as output — is that what you had in mind?
author: baskaryan

body:
> @ashleyxuu added a `generate_df` method that takes dataframes as input and returns dataframes as output — is that what you had in mind?

Yes, exactly. But the problem is: `generate_df` and `_generate` methods will then return a `bigframes.pandas.DataFrame` type rather than `LLMResult` type. However, the LLMChain class needs a `LLMResult` type to get it run or invoke. Any ideas about that? Should I redefine a BigFramesChain?
author: ashleyxuu

author: eyurtsev

body:
Hi @eyurtsev ,

not sure about what you are saying - but also haven't been on this issue for some time.

The function is called `parse_input` and according to the typing it should also be able to handle strings (which makes sense in some cases where an LLM might be return some function signature), but then when handing a string, the function doesn't seem to work and also in the tests no such case is covered. 

So why not just make it work? One way or another, we get a nice handy pydantic model, that we can work with in the following steps.
author: gutzbenj

body:
Hi @gutzbenj, the name of the function should be updated, the string parsing there is for backwards compatibility with old style tools that accepted a single input from an LLM that was formatted as a string.

These days folks often rely on dedicated tool calling APIs that allow LLMs to return structured information rather than strings.

We could create an opt-in way of specifying the tool expects the input as a string and even specify one or more supported encodings (e.g., JSON or YAML) -- I just don't want the code to be doing this on the default path without any opt-in since it creates ambiguity in terms of how to interpret the input

body:
`Open question: How to deal with this best in RunnableSequence/RunnableMap? The next steps in the sequence are probably not designed to handle the reset marker, should RunnableSequence retry all steps after "current" once it sees a retry marker?`

Are the options:

1) RunnableSequence stops as soon as it sees a reset marker and kicks off a retry
2) RunnableSequence sees a reset marker, makes sure it is propagated through all the steps and then kicks off a retry

Could runnables declare that they support the reset marker and if so, they would receive a reset marker if part of a runnable sequence?

What problems do we think users might bump into? e.g., runnable appending streaming content to a file (not for logging purposes) and can't clean up?

----

For astream log, do we need a correlation id for reset markers?

body:
hi @eyurtsev thanks for having a look at this.
I initially had multprocessing implmented, check the commit history or first commit: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/11598/commits/e9d38bb3538b6681dc9b6d0266b7932c2c7bc156

But multiprocessing actually slows things down if a tokenizer is used as length function (e.g. huggingface or tiktoken) as they use multithreading which is incompatible with multiprocessing in this case.

That's why I switched to multithreading and for the tests I ran it improved performance.
author: gustavz

body: @gustavz Is there any component which is IO bound rather than CPU bound? The Python GIL means that there can be no improvement in performance (only slow down) unless there is an IO component to the code (e.g., a network request, a file read etc.)
author: eyurtsev

body: @gustavz Do you have benchmarking results? Maybe the underlying code releases the gil. Whether this works or not seems highly situation specific and depends on which tokenizers are used. I can imagine processing to also work if tokenizing just with python
author: eyurtsev

body:
@eyurtsev you are right about that, this was also the reason I chose multiprocessing at first, but after testing it with tiktoken and huggingface tokenizers it showed a slow down in performance, so I switched to threading, but yeah reasonabilty is limited.
I'd say I either close this or switch back to multiprocessing if you say that's something langchain would be interested in.
author: gustavz

body: @gustavz OK we'll close for now -- we'll be tackling this likely soon anyway to make processing more efficient in general

body: @meet1919 I'm worried about the unexpected behavior if a user has defined their own `id` metadata key. @baskaryan what is the "langchain" way to do this?
author: jeffchuber
eyurtsev

body:
@jeffchuber using `_chroma_id` may solve this. User mostly wont save with this key. @eyurtsev 's idea seems more flexible by allowing for extra agruments in init method. In the `similarity_search()` method there can be a argument: `return_document_id`: `Boolean`. Toggling this value may or may not return the `_chroma_id` in the metadata.

One more out of the box solution is to change `Document` class
```python
class Document(Serializable):
    """Class for storing a piece of text and associated metadata."""

    page_content: str
    """String text."""
    metadata: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    """Arbitrary metadata about the page content (e.g., source, relationships to other
        documents, etc.).
    """
    id: str
    """Document id"""
```

author: baskaryan

body:
Hey thanks for your contribution!

> Add GetByID strategy to allow retrieving exact documents when needed

I found this a niche use-case. Have you considered keeping this strategy within your codebase and referencing it? Also did you know we support the ability to adjust the query (https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/vectorstores/elasticsearch#customise-the-query) before its sent to elasticsearch? One idea is you customise the query to do the id filter

> Update ElasticsearchStore to allow loading data from an index that does not follow the Langchain index structure by
> remapping them.

This could be a nice addition to the API but I do wonder if its a retriever that you want rather than customising the Store. We dont yet maintain a good retriever but definitely something we want to build soon.

> Fix store to return None for page_content when the field is missing, preventing hardfails if a specific document is
> malformed.
 
This is a nice bug fix. Would you be happy adding this as a separate PR?
author: joemcelroy

body:
@joemcelroy 

Hey, thank you for the quick feedback! Yes def. a niche use case and something that lives in our codebase now, wanted to see if it was potentially useful to others but you are correct that they can probably solve with the the query rewrite.

I will make a separate PR with just the bug fix. 

Do you think the functionality to remap arbitrary fields from an index into the final langchain object is worth also keeping or not something you foresee getting a lot of usage and not worth the added complexity ?
author: izo0x90

body:
> Do you think the functionality to remap arbitrary fields from an index into the final langchain object is worth also keeping or not something you foresee getting a lot of usage and not worth the added complexity ?

I haven't heard of this use-case yet but its definitely something I would like to improve (accommodate different indices schemas on langchain). 

I suggest creating an issue in github and we can monitor votes for such feature before we add it to ElasticsearchStore.

body:
@volodymyr-memsql  thanks for the contribution! Main thing is adding sanitizastion to all the SQL queries. 

Here's a reference on how to do it:

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Connection.execute
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/19314342/python-sqlalchemy-pass-parameters-in-connection-execute

We basically don't want to use any string interpolation on the python side and instead separate params and query and let the connection execute method take care of sanitization
