body:
> AzureOpenAI supports the ability to configure headers.
> 
> https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/56653c53aae55f8638a673764c8784dca93718da/libs/langchain/langchain/llms/openai.py#L178-L179
> 
> ```python
> AzureOpenAI(
>    model_kwargs={
>             "headers": {
>             },
>         }
> )
> ```

Nice catch. However, the OpenAIEmbeddings class also allow you to set model_kwargs, while also providing the opportunity to set the headers. It can be confusing that is possible to set headers directly when using OpenAIEmbeddings but not when using AzureOpenAI. What do you think?
author: SDonkelaarGDD

body:
> Apologies for the slow review! Pr has some merge conflicts, happy to re-review if you'd like to resolve

No problem! 

I saw that the original `AzureOpenAI` class is now deprecated. The advice is to use `AzureChatOpenAI` class instead, which allows you to set headers using `default_headers`. Hence I don't think this is relevant anymore and closed the PR.

Most tools by definition allow an llm to interact with the external world via either data reads/mutations/deletions etc; that's part of the goal of connecting an agent to a tool; e.g., if an llm is given access to the file system, one SHOULD expect that it's possible for the llm by mistake to delete files. I think the issue isn't so much that the tools can't mutate state or have risks, but that the risks aren't clearly commnunicated, so we're to start addressing that.

body:
Hello @eyurtsev 

My goal is to be able to combine all the advanced features of langchain. That's impossible at the moment.

I want to be able to :
- cut a document into fragments
- for each fragment, transform them into several versions
- persist each version in a vs
- when recovering a version, recover the original fragment
- manage the lifecycle of all fragments and associated versions
- when using VS, 
  - combine SelfQueryRetriever, MultiQueryRetriever, ParentDocumentRetriever, etc.
  - combine filters
- Manage the life cycle of fragment and associated transformation with `index()`
It's that simple.

My idea is to offer a wrapper around the VS. This wrapper can be use in place of all VS.
Then, If I extend the SelfQueryRetriver, it's possible to use an equivalent of ParentDocumentRetriever, etc.

The code is not published now, but you can read a 
[notebook](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-parent/blob/master/parent_vectorstore.ipynb) 
with the ideas (see the chapter "Short version").

I will propose 
- a solution de generate multiple versions for each fragment (`DocumentTransformerPipeline` the name will be changed)
  - Generate 3 questions for the fragment
  - Summarize the fragment
  - etc.
- a VectorStoreWrapper (to be compatible with SelfQueryRetriever)
- An implementation of VectorStoreWrapper to manage multiple transformations of a fragment: `ParentVectorStore`

I think it's possible to enrich LCEL to introduce these new ideas:
- Combine transformations with a pipe
- etc.

What are your thoughts on this?

body:
> cut a document into fragments
> for each fragment, transform them into several versions
> persist each version in a vs
> when recovering a version, recover the original fragment
> manage the lifecycle of all fragments and associated versions
> when using VS,
> combine SelfQueryRetriever, MultiQueryRetriever, ParentDocumentRetriever, etc.
> combine filters
> Manage the life cycle of fragment and associated transformation with index()
> It's that simple.

I don't know that storing all the information in the same vectorstore will be possible with all vectorstores. Some ofthe vectorstores are limited in terms of which operations they support and what kind of data can be stored in them.

Would a document store that can keep track of document content and metadata, and allows basic operations together with read, write, list based on metadata  + a layer that supports caching intermediate processing results support this use case? This would allow fetch the relevant data (potentially cached) and index it into an arbitrary vectorstore?

> I think it's possible to enrich LCEL to introduce these new ideas:
> 
> Combine transformations with a pipe

We've considered doing this, but we haven't pushed on it yet, some of the issues that needed to be worked out:

1) Unclear that a document pipeline should leverage LCEL syntax -- would need an obvious benefit (e.g., async support out of the box)
2) If using LCEL need to figure out the following issues:
 -- Existing loader interface takes all via __init__ , not load, which doesn't play nicely with runnables. Can do tricks like `DocumentLoaderClass.as_runnable( init params )` to workaround, but it does add complexity
-- Needs to handle memory consumption
-- May need to handle multi threading and multi processing optimizations

body:
@eyurtsev

I strongly urge you to look at the [notebook](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/rag_vectorstore.ipynb). It completely demonstrates all the advantages of full integration of langchain features.

# RagVectorStore

> I don't know that storing all the information in the same vectorstore will be possible with all vectorstores. Some ofthe vectorstores are limited in terms of which operations they support and what kind of data can be stored in them.

Like the [ParentDocumentRetriever](https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/retrievers/parent_document_retriever), I combine a `VectorStore` and a `DocStore`. The code is [here](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/rag_vectorstore.py).

The new version of the notebook is [here](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/rag_vectorstore.ipynb).

For a complete integration, with all advanced features, I propose to add some objects:
- A [MemoryRecordManager](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/indexes/memory_recordmanager.py)
- A [SQLStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/storage/sql_docstore.py)
- A generic VectorStore wrapper [WrapperVectorStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/wrapper_vectorstore.py)
- And, at the end, the [RagVectorStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/rag_vectorstore.py)

Why is important?
- `MemoryRecordManager` is for test, a demo, or working all in memory with `index()` or `aindex()`
- `SQLStore` is if you want to merge the VectorStore, the DocStore and the RecordManager in the same database (maybe with the compatibility with a unique transaction), it may be possible to reuse the engine. A first implementation is [here](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/rag_vectorstore.py#L549). I will propose to accept an optional `vectorstore`.
- `WrapperVectorStore` is to be compatible with [SelfQueryRetriever](https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/data_connection/retrievers/self_query). With this wrapper, it's possible to add the class in [`_get_builtin_translator()`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/0da75b9ebd1e5a485a295d6f519f2d7be1f89f0a/libs/langchain/langchain/retrievers/self_query/base.py#L51). At the moment I'm using a [hack](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/wrapper_vectorstore.py#L205). Then, the `RagVectorStore` can use other's `VectorStore` with `SelfQueryRetriever`. Another advantage for developers is that when the VectorStore interface evolves, the wrappers generally remain compatible. Eventually, it is necessary to review the overloaded methods that have modified their signatures.

# LCEL with Transformer
In my implementation, I propose an optional approach to use LCEL with Transformer. 
You can read the unit test [here](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/tests/unittests/document_transformers/test_runnable_transformers.py#L120) and the code [here](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/document_transformers/runnable_document_transformer.py)

> We propose an alternative way of making transformers compatible with LCEL.
>    The first keeps the current protocol (RunnableDocumentTransformer).
>    The second takes advantage of this to propose
>    a lazy approach to transformations (RunnableGeneratorDocumentTransformer).
>    It's better for the memory, pipeline, etc.
    
>    Now, it's possible to create a pipeline of transformer like:
>    Example:
```python
    class UpperTransformer(RunnableGeneratorDocumentTransformer):
        def lazy_transform_documents(
                self,
                documents: Iterator[Document],
                **kwargs: Any
        ) -> Iterator[Document]:
            ...

        async def alazy_transform_documents(
                self,
                documents: Union[AsyncIterator[Document],Iterator[Document]],
                **kwargs: Any
        ) -> AsyncIterator[Document]:
            ...

    runnable = (UpperTransformer() | LowerTransformer())
    result = list(runnable.invoke(documents))
```
If you accept my future pull-request, you will have to review all the Transformer subclasses.

# LCEL with retriever
May be, it's possible to propose a syntax to chain the retrievers.
```python
vs.as_retriever() | EmbeddingsFilter(...) | ContextualCompressionRetriever(...)
```
# Pull-request
At this time, I must add some tests. Then I would like to propose one or multiple pull-request:
- One for the [MemoryRecordManager](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/indexes/memory_recordmanager.py) ([PR #13200](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/13200))
- One for the [SQLStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/storage/sql_docstore.py) ([PR #13181](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/13181))
- One for [WrapperVectorStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/wrapper_vectorstore.py) ([PR #13190](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/13190))
- One for the [first integration](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/document_transformers/runnable_document_transformer.py) of LCEL
- And the last one for [RagVectorStore](https://github.com/pprados/langchain-rag/blob/master/langchain_rag/vectorstores/rag_vectorstore.py)

But, it's very complicated to maintain this for each new version. I've already suffered a lot with Google Drive or qa_with_reference integration.

Perhaps you can encourage me in my approach and allow me to have more direct access, in order to complete this proposal as quickly as possible?

@eyurtsev, what would be the most effective communication channel?

body:
@joemcelroy 
First of all, thank you for your guidance.

As you mentioned above, I proceeded with 3 tasks.

1. restored the position of `rrf` argument.
2. added optional `fetch_k` argument in similarity_search().
3. added test code `test_similarity_search_approx_with_hybrid_search_rrf()` in TestElasticsearch class.

but implementation of "1. restored the position of `rrf` argument" is a little bit different.
You mentioned `rrf=False`, I changed it as `rrf={"rank_constant": 1, "window_size": 5}`

The reason is that I thought the users can pass the rrf parameters(rank_constant, window_size).

If you think this implementation is not profer, pz let me know how to fix it.
author: HwangJohn

body:
I see, I thought you just wanted to switch rrf off, which was a reasonable request. Being able to provide configuration to `rrf` is a good idea too!

So i support that rrf can either be a boolean or a dict. 

- By default its true and when true,  its`rrf: {}`
- When false, `rrf` is not part of the request and is omitted
- When a dict, pass in the dict values to the `rrf` key. Example: 

```python
    strategy=ElasticsearchStore.ApproxRetrievalStrategy(
        hybrid=True,
        rrf={"rank_constant": 1, "window_size": 5}
    )

    strategy=ElasticsearchStore.ApproxRetrievalStrategy(
        hybrid=True,
        rrf=True # default value
    )

    strategy=ElasticsearchStore.ApproxRetrievalStrategy(
        hybrid=True,
        rrf=False
    )
 ```

body:
Hi @eyurtsev,

Thank you for your quick response. Yes, I would support adding a commit() call somewhere as well. I apologise if I seem vague, we found this issue back in June.
I've reproduced the bug so you can take a look. It occurs when we try to construct a PGVector vector store by itself, rather than using the from_documents method found in the same PGVector class as shown below. In this scenario, the default collection has already been created and filled with vectors by the way.

```
File "/Users/bmo/Documents/projects/gpt-knowledgebase-chat/source/lib/vectorstore/postgresql/postgresql_vectorstore_adapter.py", line 56, in __init__
  self._vector_store = PGVector(
File "/Users/bmo/Documents/projects/gpt-knowledgebase-chat/source/lib/langchain/vectorstores/pgvector.py", line 139, in __init__
  self.__post_init__()
File "/Users/bmo/Documents/projects/gpt-knowledgebase-chat/source/lib/langchain/vectorstores/pgvector.py", line 149, in __post_init__
  self.create_tables_if_not_exists()
File "/Users/bmo/Documents/projects/gpt-knowledgebase-chat/source/lib/langchain/vectorstores/pgvector.py", line 168, in create_tables_if_not_exists
  self._conn.commit()
AttributeError: 'Connection' object has no attribute 'commit'
```

Hi @eyurtsev ,
Thank you for the review. I agree with your points. I will try to put the similarity score within similarity_score_threshold function.

Also regarding the questions
1.  We are updating the metadata of the doc dynamically with "score" as the key, so that we can use that for downstream apps
      ' doc.metadata = {**doc.metadata, **{"score": score}} ' helps us achieve that.
      
2. To the second question,  we can use a unique key name and mention in the docs, so that users will choose some other key. As you mentioned we can give the parameter "score_key" as kwargs and write some condition and raise ValueError on invalid combination. 

Will work on these changes and update
author: sethusaim

body:
One question what combinations should we allow the user to control ....for example - 
1. The user wants to filter based on the threshold - default option which is already there
2. The user wants to filter based on the threshold and wants the score of returned docs -  currently not sending any score
3. The user wants to get the scores of all the docs without threshold 

Also appending the score in metadata seemed like a better option since it can be treated as unique key like  
how we have for source, etc  [ which the user not explicity change ]. If the user does not want the "score" key, it is fine and he can choose to use it.
Ofcourse we can implement this without having a new search type

This looks awesome! Are there any security concerns with executing LLM generated cube queries? if so would prefer to move the chain and agent to langchain_experimental and add some security warnings to the docstring and docs

cc @MikeNitsenko @eyurtsev
author: baskaryan

body:
> This looks awesome! Are there any security concerns with executing LLM generated cube queries? if so would prefer to move the chain and agent to langchain_experimental and add some security warnings to the docstring and docs
> 
> cc @MikeNitsenko @eyurtsev

It is not susceptible to SQL Injection and is not affected by other security issues.
- The queries can only utilize metadata defined within the cube. If the LLM generates non-existent metadata, data retrieval will not be possible.
- The Cube does not support  created, modified, or deleted operations.

@baskaryan
author: johnmai-dev

body:
Hi @maiqingqiang thank you for the contribution! Code quality is great, so we can definitely merge.

Before the merge we need to add in code documentation + security note. Documentation should go for the agent/chain/tools -- OK to duplicate. 

Things to document:
* Uses rest API to interact with the data
* Include link to API spec:  https://cube.dev/docs/reference/rest-api
* Explain the API does (e.g., offers read only queries over the data -- if that's true).
* Say in the security note that that a user can potentially access any of the data that's avaiable

Is there any row level security provided for the data? For example, if I were to upload an orders tables with customer ids, is there a way to safely run queries on behalf of a particular customer (without seeing any other customer data?)


nits: 
* Could you update the code to use `*` prior to any named arguments?
* If you're able to provide any unit-tests that would be appreciated, but is not required.

author: baskaryan

body:
Hi @baskaryan , thanks for the reply.
For llm level, as the `llms.OpenAIChat` uses `openai.chatCompletions` while `llms.OpenAI` uses `openai.chat`, the latter one should be deprecated which is requesting `/completions` (the former one requests latest `/chat/completions`).
That's the main reason I raised this PR.

As for `ChatOpenAI`, that's the chat model level API, not on llm level. In some popular LLM applications , the are still rely on llm level but not the chat model level API.

Back to discussion about `CardList` in the index pages.

CardList makes sense [here](https://integrations.langchain.com/tools) where each card has a practical features as buttons to get to the Doc, GitHub. It has a popularity icon and the company logo. Card helps is the integration research/discovery by having those additional elements.
Now, how does in work here in the `Componenets/document_loaders` [page](https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/document_loaders)? 
Here it is just a bad copy of ToC (the original ToC is on the sidebar). Why is it bad?
1. bad to search. It is too big to scroll down. A user would use the sidebar ToC to search for a particular item.
2. bad for discovery. It holds a short chunk of the description text. It doesn't get any additional means to discovery (how it is on the above `integrations` site). Moreover, the description text is cut in the most cards.
3. is it beautiful? No? It does not fit the site design.

The main question is `why do we have another ToC`? `We need more cleaning, not more clogging.`

As a simple test, I've tried:

```
import asyncio
import boto3

from langchain_community.llms import Bedrock
from langchain.schema.output_parser import StrOutputParser
from langchain.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate

model = Bedrock(client=client, model_id="anthropic.claude-v2:1")
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("Tell me a story about {topic}.")
parser = StrOutputParser()

async def main():
    chain = prompt | model | parser
    async for chunk in chain.astream({"topic": "bears"}):
        print(chunk)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

@DLOVRIC2 
I tested your changes with the example code you had provided, and it seemed to work well for the streaming use case. Pending, response on my earlier question about blocking async call for non-streaming responses, I think the code looks good otherwise and we should merge with what we have so far. There are a few things to point out, that we can improve in the next iteration.

1. `prepare_output_stream` and `aprepare_output_stream` are identical in their content, it would be nice if we can avoid duplication in them; I couldn't figure this out yet because they return different iterators.
2. This change only targets the non-chat LLM class, having similar changes in `BedrockChat` will be desirable.
3. I started looking at [aiobotocore](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiobotocore) but need more research into it's Bedrock implementation and how the client will be disposed. Most examples are using context manager for client creation, so not clear on how this should be handled if we create one client per LLM instance. Using `aiobotocore` library will help us simplify some of the code here, and allow true async for service connections as @andrewkcarter mentioned.

body:
Hey @slangenbach, thanks for working on this. I am getting the following error when I try to generate a devcontainer on GitHub Codespaces.

Will this PR fix the issue or should a create an issue too?

```
2330.6 Terminated
------
Dockerfile-with-features:46
--------------------
  44 |     
  45 |     # Install the Poetry dependencies (this layer will be cached as long as the dependencies don't change)
  46 | >>> RUN poetry install --no-interaction --no-ansi --with dev,test,docs
  47 |     
  48 |     FROM $_DEV_CONTAINERS_BASE_IMAGE AS dev_containers_target_stage
--------------------
ERROR: failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c poetry install --no-interaction --no-ansi --with dev,test,docs" did not complete successfully: exit code: 143
ERROR: Service 'langchain' failed to build : Build failed
```
author: sdelgadoc

body:
@sdelgadoc Yes with the caveat that my fix doesn't install dependencies for docs. If this is strictly required, I'll look into it. 

Docs' dependencies are listed in the pyproject.toml file at the root of the project. I focus on dependencies required for development specified in pyproject.toml at /libs/langchain

body:
Hi, thanks for opening this!

I'm curious and wanted to learn more about the threat model you are considering for this PR.

In order for the `NotStrLike` value to be used and cause the issue in your repro, some piece of code needed to construct it. If so, that piece of code called some presumably-arbitrary attacker-controlled code and already is in trouble, since the attack payload may equivalently have been inside `NotStrLike.__init__()` instead of in `NotStrLike.__fspath__()`.

In that case, merging this PR doesn't prevent the problem since the underlying issue happens before `langchain` is ever involved — at the time where the user's code first touched the malicious `NotStrLike` class.

Hey @leo-gan - I feel like the listings are actually relatively useful on a lot of these pages. For example, after reading about comparison evaluators, my logical next step is to read about a specific one.

Completely hear you that it's duplicate information if you have the sidebar open as well, but I don't think it hurts to have the cards (I tend to use the cards instead of navigating the sidebar when they're available).

Happy to discuss!
author: efriis

body:
@efriis I agree; it could add value to some index pages. Especially if the index page text is short and the number of items in the ToC is not big or small. 
But it is completely useless if the number of items is small (<3-5). It is harmful if the number of items is large (>20).
So, it is hard to make it in consistent way. Sometimes it helps, sometimes it is useless, and sometimes it is harmful.
Consistency is important. Inconsistency harms reading comprehension. Now this DocCardList is inconsistent, it is placed on some index pages without a system.
That is logic behind this PR.
Cons: index pages with a small amount of text look ... so-so. (I'd rather add more text there.)

IMHO, for now, placing `DocCardList` makes sense only in the fully generated index pages. And even in this case, `DocCardList` is helpful only if the text on these cards is prepared and formatted properly.
author: leo-gan

body:
Agreed on the large number side, but on the small number, they act as a pretty good call to action of where to go next.

Given the numbers of subpages are pretty reasonable on these pages, would you be ok skipping this set? Fully agreed it might be worth removing on some other pages.

body:
I have added one more test and fixed the name of the existing test (removed the "fails" from the name). I propose to merge this PR as is, since it is an improvement that avoids duplication of the original text in the output :-) But, the problem of scrambling the _order_ of the output is still very confusing, as soon as slightly more complex html with different tags is processed. First all `

` tags are read (skipping other tags and excluding the text from the inner `

  • `, `
    `, `` tags), and then all the `
  • ` and `
    ` tags are rendered, and later all the `` tags, so a very confusing end result text will be rendered: all `
  • `, `
    ` and `` tags are pulled out of their original `

    ` context and lumped together at the end. I am not sure how useful such text would even be for training of inference (unless we are doing "bag of words" ML). Anyway, #LGTM. That out-of-order problem can be fixed in a next iteration (I have some ideas).
author: petervandenabeele

body:
Yesss, we cracked it :-)

This is a correct implementation that:
* extract each wanted tag only once without duplicates
* keeps the original text in order
* keeps clean single spaces between consecutive extracted tags
* has a number of green tests for more complex cases (no more failing tests)

The trick was to:

* not loop over the tags like the previous implementation, but
* loop over the tags
* recursively get all navigable strings (using the implementation of @nfcampos , thanks for that :-)
* and then, once a "parent" tags is extracted, _decompose_ it, so that all it's descendants are not _again_ extracted

With the correct implementation, suddenly all my tests turned green at once, Yeehaa :-)

Thanks for the collaboration on this @nfcampos :-)

Your review would be appreciated @baskaryan .

body:
Hi, thanks for opening the PR. Out of curiosity, what does having the automatic comments accomplish here? Is there a use case or situation that isn't appropriately handled at the moment that this PR resolves?

Every bit of code we adopt has some maintenance cost, especially in situations where we need to hand our GitHub token to new actions. It's good to consider the benefits vs maintenance tradeoff, and I'd like to understand the use case for this PR better.
author: obi1kenobi

body: Automatic comments in a pull request (PR) offer benefits like providing context, inline feedback, integration with tools, automation for code quality, and visibility. However, it's crucial to weigh these benefits against the maintenance effort, including managing tokens and relevance. The decision to use automatic comments should align with project goals and specific needs.

body:
This pull request works, but the examples need updating to include location.  Location is a required parameter for Model Garden endpoints:

```python
from langchain.llms import VertexAIModelGarden
from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate

project_id="my-project"
location="us-central1"
endpoint_id="1589614531232312313"

# broken, fixed in PR
# https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/12723
llm = VertexAIModelGarden(project=project_id, endpoint_id=endpoint_id, location=location)

prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("What is the meaning of {thing}?")

chain = prompt | llm
print(chain.invoke({"thing": "life"}))
#Prompt:
#What is the meaning of life?
#Output:
# It is a question that has puzzled philosophers, theologians, scient
```

body:
Current PR breaks if pipeline_kwargs are directly passed in HuggingFacePipeline:
```python
from langchain import HuggingFacePipeline
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline

pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model='gpt2', max_new_tokens=100)
hf = HuggingFacePipeline(pipeline=pipe, pipeline_kwargs={"temperature": 0.3})

# expected:
hf.pipeline_kwargs == {'temperature': 0.3}
# actual:
hf.pipeline_kwargs == {'max_new_tokens': 100}
```

Either pipeline_kwargs shouldn't be passed when transformers pipeline is passed, or there should be some function that figures out all arguments passed in both the transformers pipe and langchaing pipe, both at init and inference, like [Pipeline._sanitize_parameters](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/07e3454f034b4889925621e8e3253547d2a04aa7/src/transformers/pipelines/text_generation.py#L110) from huggingface.

body:
works for me... would it be better to just "match" the underlying API though?

eg

```
def get(self, include=['ids']) -> List[str]:
        """Returns all Documents that are currently present in the collection
        Returns:
            List[str]: list of all ids currently present in the collection
        """
        return self.get(include=include)
```
(also add `where`, etc?) 

Or... @timonpalm you can also do this - by passing in the Chroma client directly, it makes it really use to use it's direct API too.

```
import chromadb

persistent_client = chromadb.PersistentClient()
collection = persistent_client.get_or_create_collection("collection_name")
collection.add(ids=["1", "2", "3"], documents=["a", "b", "c"])

langchain_chroma = Chroma(
    client=persistent_client,
    collection_name="collection_name",
    embedding_function=embedding_function,
)

collection.get.... 

print("There are", langchain_chroma._collection.count(), "in the collection")
```

This is most preferable as I think as it minimizes the code that needs to be maintained.

Tasks Performed:

-> HTML Content Extraction: Updated the code to extract HTML content from email messages.
-> OTP Code Extraction: Added a feature to identify and extract OTP codes from HTML content.
-> Code Refactoring: Improved code structure, variable names, and comments for clarity.
-> New Response Fields: Added "html_content" and "otp_code" to the tool's response.

Issues Resolved:

-> HTML Content Handling: Resolved the limitation of processing only plain text, now supporting both plain text and HTML content.
-> OTP Code Extraction: Added the ability to find and extract OTP codes from email messages.

New Dependencies:

-> Regular Expressions (re): Introduced the re module for working with regular expressions.

These updates enhance the tool's functionality, improve code readability, and enable OTP code extraction from HTML content.

body: When the agent is created, it creates the tools (`Tool` model) by calling `Tool.from_function` and sets the description, this is then passed to LLM. If I change the description on `E2BDataAnalysisTool` it won't propagate to `Tool`, because you have to pass when calling `Tool.from_function`. TBH not sure everything we do is the best way, maybe there's better way? Would it be possible to have `E2BDataAnalysisTool` as superclass of `Tool`? But it seems it isn't supposed to be done this way anymore.

body:
> This is actually coming from the fact that the Redis semantic cache overrides the `content_key` with `prompt`
> 
> see:
> 
> https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/8e0cb2eb84539b249198f98f7647a1f24b2392c2/libs/langchain/langchain/cache.py#L444
> 
> and the `similarity_search_with_scores` doesn't use `getattr` for the `content_key` like the `..by_vector` does.
> 
> And so the correct way to fix this is to do
> 
> ```python
> doc = Document(page_content=getattr(result, self._schema.content_key),
>                metadata=metadata)
> ```
> 
> See `Redis.similarity_search_by_vector` for the example.

Thank you for your feedback and suggested changes.
When I can't find this attribute, I should indeed think about reflection.

body: This looks good! And thanks for fixing. body:
@baskaryan This parameter has a different utility than the idea of user_agent you have in mind, and it doesn't make sense to make it opt-in.  MongoClient has 2 optional parameters 'appname' and 'driver'. The user_agent functionality probably maps to the appname field, and its left up to the user to use however they see fit. The 'driver' field is used in driver implemented on top of PyMongo

```
appname: (string or None) The name of the application that created this MongoClient instance. The server will log this value upon establishing each connection. It is also recorded in the slow query log and profile collections.

driver: (pair or None) A driver implemented on top of PyMongo can pass a 'DriverInfo' to add its name, version, and platform to the message printed in the server log when establishing a connection.
```
https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/mongo_client.html

body:
@dosuken123 I am trying your fix and it doesn't seem to work for minor `openai` versions such as `1.0.0b3`.  This comparison is returning `False` in that case:
![image](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/assets/136352541/692779f4-a1f7-4e33-aca7-a545976f0247)

I modified your fix to compare major version directly like so, and it seems to work:
```
def is_openai_v1() -> bool:
    _version = parse(version("openai"))
    return _version.major >= 1
```

EDIT:  once I get past this check, there are other problems with the beta release of openai I'm using (`1.0.0b3`).

body: This does not seem to solve the rate limit error when using chromaDB and ada002 to embed. I still got the same RateLimitError (even though the requests we were doing were well below our ratelimit). Using Chroma default embedding function "all-MiniLM-L6-v2" seems to work.
author: afmurillo

body:
The ratelimit is imposed by OpenAI (or Azure). So this won't remove it. But
instead of retrying every 4 sec for example, you can override the default
values. For example in my case when I trigger an  RateLimitError , the
message indicates I have to wait 40 sec, so I set the min to 40sec. Like
that I know it won't retry until 40 sec.
--
Alex

body:
Hey @akashAD98 ! These templates are a bit different than notebooks. They have some unique requirements about their format outlined [here](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/templates/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md).

In this particular case, you're testing with the old `.run` interface, which LangServe doesn't use (it uses the new LCEL `.ainvoke` `.astream` and `abatch` instead).

Would you prefer to upload this as an example notebook as part of the LanceDB docs at https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/vectorstores/lancedb ?

For support getting LangServe/templates set up to be able to test your PRs, discord is probably the best forum! If you get set up, happy to take another look. Otherwise, I'll probably close this PR because it won't work for users :(

or even better, -> `LanguageModelInput = Union[PromptValue, str, BaseMessage]` and `ChatModelInput=Union[LanguageModelInput, List[BaseMessage]]`

body:
> and just thinking out loudly, maybe make `LanguageModelInput = Union[PromptValue, str, List[BaseMessage]]` -> `LanguageModelInput = Union[PromptValue, str, BaseMessage, List[BaseMessage]]` or even better, -> `LanguageModelInput = Union[PromptValue, str, BaseMessage]` and `ChatModelInput=Union[LanguageModelInput, List[BaseMessage]]`
> 
> Since if a user wants to pass a text + image(s) to a LLM, they should pass it as a BaseMessage (or a HumanMessage), not as a list of messages.

Text + images here would be sub-message, meaning a single message would have 1 or more parts, 1 of which would contain image content


Will probably land this #14263 , which builds on this pr

body:
@baskaryan 
If you think this PR is satisfactory, could you assist me with the linting issue? The error message is as follows:
```python
langchain/retrievers/multi_field.py:102: error: Item "BaseRetriever" of "Union[BaseRetriever, VectorStore]" has no attribute "from_documents"  [union-attr]
tests/unit_tests/retrievers/test_multi_field.py:25: error: Argument "retriever" to "from_documents" of "MultiFieldRetriever" has incompatible type "Type[TFIDFRetriever]"; expected 
```

In code 
```python
    @classmethod
    def from_documents(
        cls,
        retriever: Union[BaseRetriever, VectorStore],
        documents: List[Document],
        meta_data_keys: List[str] = [],
        search_kwargs: dict = {},
        str_concat_func: Callable = _create_content_and_metadata,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> BaseRetriever:
 
        Returns:
            BaseRetriever: An instance of MultiFieldRetriever with the underlying
            retriever initialized with the processed documents.
        """
        pseudo_doc_list = [
            Document(
                page_content=str_concat_func(doc, meta_data_keys),
                metadata={"doc": doc},
            )
            for doc in documents
        ]

        retriever = retriever.from_documents(documents=pseudo_doc_list, **kwargs)
        if isinstance(retriever, VectorStore):
            return cls(retriever=retriever.as_retriever(search_kwargs=search_kwargs))
        return cls(retriever=retriever)
```

For the argument `retriever`, I intended to allow any subclass of `VectorStore`, such as `FAISS`, or any subclass of `Retriever`, such as `BM25Retriever`. However, it seems that the type hint is incorrect.

body:
Hey @Toubat appreciate the PR! We actually had something like this a bit ago but removed because it seemed redundant / wasn't really being used #12133

i think the RunnablePassthrough.assign method has really helped with cases like this as well. what do you think of something like this for the example you provided?

```python
from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate
from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.schema import StrOutputParser
from langchain.schema.runnable import RunnablePassthrough

prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("{context} {question}")
llm = ChatOpenAI()


retriever = (lambda _: ["doc 1 ...", "doc n"])  # mock retriever

def _format(input):
    return "## Documents" + "\n\n".join(x for x in input["context"])

answer_chain = (
    RunnablePassthrough.assign(context=_format) | prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()
)
retrieval_chain =  (
    {"context": retriever, "question": RunnablePassthrough(),}
    | RunnablePassthrough.assign(answer=answer_chain)
)

retrieval_chain.invoke("say foo")
```

body:
Hey @baskaryan, thanks for providing more insights on this! I believe there is some overlap between the current PR and the `PutLocalVar` and `GetLocaVar`. Regarding `RunnablePassthrough.assign`, it works pretty well on some cases where the previous piped chain is a map (so that we can use `RunnablePassthrough.assign` to merge the key values). 

What I'm more interested is that if there is a way that allows to connect data from the very earlier stage of the chain pipeline to the very end stage of the chain pipeline (without the need to passing data in the intermediate chain stages). In addition, to use `RunnablePassthrough.assign` I believe we have to connect it with map before this chain, which might not be generic enough for some cases. A simple example to illustrate.

Suppose I have a quite long chain below:
```python
core_data = lambda x: get_core_data(x)

chain = chain_op_1 
| chain_op_2 
| core_data 
| chain_op_3
| chain_op_4
| 
... 
| 
chain_op_n 
| { "result": RunnablePassthrough() }
```

Now, for some reason I want to update the chain by keeping track of inner data and store that as part of output. Suppose we want to get `core_data` output into the final answer:
```python
{ "result": RunnablePassthrough(), "core_data": <want to get core_data here> }
```

I can get the sense of how to allow this using `RunnablePassthrough.assign` with
```python
core_data = lambda x: get_core_data(x)

chain = {
    "core_data": chain_op_1 | chain_op_2 | core_data 
}
| RunnablePassthrough.assign(
    result=itemgetter("core_data") | chain_op_3 | chain_op_4 | ... | chain_op_n 
)
```

The problem I have is, the mental model of using `RunnablePassthrough.assign` with the above implementation isn't quite straightforward, partially due to the reason that 
1. The final result dict schema isn't been explicitly written by me, which makes me struggled a while trying to figure out what the output dict would look like. This issue would become worse as we stack more and more RunnablePassthrough.assign in a row, like  
```python
RunnablePassthrough.assign(a=...) | RunnablePassthrough.assign(b=...) | RunnablePassthrough.assign(c=...) ..
```
 
2. Even adding a simple data passage across pipeline requires the rewritten of the chain, which wouldn't hurt for small chains but might be a huge refactor for longer and more complex chain. Similar feeling for
```python
retrieval_chain =  (
    {"context": retriever, "question": RunnablePassthrough(),}
    | RunnablePassthrough.assign(answer=answer_chain)
)
```
At the first glance, I wouldn't know the final answer should be a dict of `{"context": ..., "question": ..., "answer": ...}`.

An example of using `RunnableContextProvider` would become:
```python
core_data = lambda x: get_core_data(x)

@context_provider
def chain(getter, setter):
    return chain_op_1 
    | chain_op_2 
    | core_data 
    | setter("core_data")
    | chain_op_3
    | chain_op_4
    | 
    ... 
    | 
    chain_op_n 
    | { "result": RunnablePassthrough(), "core_data": getter("core_data") }
```

This makes minimal change of the original chain structure and looks more clear of what exactly I want to accomplish. I believe the benefit of having some data injection mechanism like `RunnableContextProvider` is that it allows enabling data sharing without the needs to make significant modification on the original chaining structure. Data sharing across different part of pipeline should be a plug-and-play ideally.

thanks for opening this, its very well thought out.

we'd explicitly made the retriever interface only take in a string on purpose. we're chatting on this internally to discuss whether it is worth changing or not.

just so i best understand - what types of different tags would you want to pass to the retriever? how would those be determined?
author: hwchase17

body:
Hi Harrison - thanks for looking at this.

On your first point: You say you've "explicitly made the retriever interface only take in a string on purpose", but in fact  (as it stands, without this PR) the Retriever _does_ allow the filter I'm using - via `search_kwargs` - just that they can only be provided  at  _construction_ rather than at query time. So it's just the "query-time" interface that is currently limited to the natural language string.

But search_kwargs are more naturally part of the query than they are part of the retriever configuration. They allow the RAG query to be hybrid: NL question + where clause.

Use cases:

 My use case is pretty simple and quite general:   Various RAG conversations with a single vector database holding many different ingested documents of different topics, with retrieval strictly _limited to a subset of the documents/vectors_ - by a traditional where clause.

If a user wishes to talk about **topicA,** I don't want to rely solely on the vector similarity to prevent context being retrieved from documents that were identified as being **topicB.** But nor do I want to have to use separate databases for these.

My specific case is tags for categories, but it's important to note that _**this PR is not about tags at all - but it makes retrieval queries support hybrid for any vector store.**_

Specific - tags: 

I'm using a single vector database (a single ChromaDB collection in this case, but it generalizes) into which I (or my users) ingest various documents, _providing tags to categorize them_ as they do.  Through my API and admin UI, I have users doing what amounts to:

 - ingest : document_a.pdf and document_b.pdf with tags "topic1" and "category_x"
 - ingest:  document_u.pdf and document_v.txt with tags "topic2" and "category_x"

etc...

Now when the user comes to converse ConversationalRetrievalChain via my API, they set indicate the topics they want: if they specify they're discussing "topic1" and "category_x" then I create a filter for that. The filter depends on the vector database, but for Chroma, I convert my tags to dicts like {"tag_{tagname}": 1}.
then when they want to use topics "topic1" and "category_x" this becomes a filter query (in Chroma syntax)
```
   {"$and": [{"tag_topic1": 1], ["tag_category_x": 1]}
```
 (this is non-ideal, and may be simpler when I come to implement it for other vector databases, but Chroma doesn't have an operator for intersecting sets, hence my use of 1/0 for each tag, when what I really want is "tag-list contains  'topic1' and 'category_x')

In my results, I show sources, and they're  limited to those that have both tags. If I just pass 'category_x' or no tag at all, I get a broader set of documents considered. 

General:
Tags are my specific use case, but I convert them to a general filter and allow, through the API,  general search filters to be provided at the time input is given to the conversation.



TL;DR: search_kwargs are more naturally part of the query than they are part of the retriever configuration. They allow the RAG query to be hybrid: NL question + where clause.

thanks again for taking time on this

cheers
chris

body:
@3coins see test script below...
```python
import boto3
import os

region = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION")
boto3_bedrock = boto3.client(
    service_name='bedrock-runtime',
    region_name=region,
)

from langchain.embeddings import BedrockEmbeddings

print('----------------Cohere Test----------------')
embedding_model = BedrockEmbeddings(
    client=boto3_bedrock,
    model_id="cohere.embed-english-v3",
)
output = embedding_model.embed_query("Hola mi nombre es Clay")
print(f"The embedding vector has {len(output)} values\n{output[0:3]+['...']+output[-3:]}")
output = embedding_model.embed_documents(["Hola mi nombre es Clay", "Hola mi nombre es piyush"])
print(f"The output has {len(output)} docs")

print('\n----------------Cohere Multilingual Test----------------')
embedding_model = BedrockEmbeddings(
    client=boto3_bedrock,
    model_id="cohere.embed-multilingual-v3",
)
output = embedding_model.embed_query("hello my name is clay")
print(f"The embedding vector has {len(output)} values\n{output[0:3]+['...']+output[-3:]}")
output = embedding_model.embed_documents(["hello my name is clay", "hello my name is piyush"])
print(f"The output has {len(output)} docs")

print('\n----------------Cohere Test with Kwargs----------------')
embedding_model = BedrockEmbeddings(
    client=boto3_bedrock,
    model_id="cohere.embed-english-v3",
    model_kwargs={"input_type": "search_document"}
)
output = embedding_model.embed_query("hello my name is clay")
print(f"The embedding vector has {len(output)} values\n{output[0:3]+['...']+output[-3:]}")
output = embedding_model.embed_documents(["hello my name is clay", "hello my name is piyush"])
print(f"The output has {len(output)} docs")

print('\n----------------Titan Tests----------------')
embedding_model = BedrockEmbeddings(
    client=boto3_bedrock,
    model_id="amazon.titan-embed-text-v1",
)
output = embedding_model.embed_query("hello my name is clay")
print(f"The embedding vector has {len(output)} values\n{output[0:3]+['...']+output[-3:]}")
output = embedding_model.embed_documents(["hello my name is clay", "hello my name is piyush"])
print(f"The output has {len(output)} docs")
```

body:
I have no issues with the PR.  The primary issue is that ooba has removed the old API and is strictly using an OpenAI API-compatible service now.  I originally wrote this add-on when the OpenAI API interface was not as mature and I wanted a very simple interface from langchain to local LLMs; without having to write new loaders for all of the various models (since ooba has that already.)

At this point, using the OpenAI API-compatible layer in ooba is probably a better future route since you can just `pip install openai` and use that to interface with ooba.  Though they have broken the recent openai module for local use in some ways (even if you set your OPENAI_API_BASE, it will still ping OAI for some calls like getting a list of the models.) So, you may want to stay with `pip install openai==0.28.1` to use the old version.

The change is simple. In my exp (Linux) textgen vary a lot from env to env depending in your OS / Hardware, i'm in particular using an old revision in which I have a balance with drivers and python libraries and I only update it time to time, since every time it's pretty painful to get it working at a proper performance  / stability.
I recommend we need to update clearly the documentation to define which version this change will support and what the last stable version compatible with the legacy textgen implementation.
This way we can save a lot of headaches to people in diff envs.

body:
Ah I see the issue. I misunderstood the case this was handling. Appreciate the explanation! Just brain dumping:

If you call `ainvoke` on a RunnableLambda that generates another RunnableLambda, that lambda will end up getting synchronously invoked in the asyncio event loop logic.

This PR solves this problem by bypassing that delegation, generating an `afunc` that does the same thing, which can then be `ainvoke`'d in the proper way.

Reopening, and going to think about if there's a good way of doing this without setting `afunc` on initialization, maybe by computing afunc within `ainvoke` if the attribute isn't set.

body:
>Do you see this behavior consistently? Do you have an example call to OpenAI that would return this?
>
>When I try to reproduce, I consistently get 'arguments': '{}'

The behavior is inconsistent. Here's some fairly minimal code that reproduces this for me:

```
def _build_no_arg_functions(name_desc: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> List[Dict]:
    return [
        {
            "name": x[0],
            "description": x[1],
            "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": [],},
        } for x in name_desc
    ]

off_topic_prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
    [
        (
            "system",
            """
I will show you a question that someone asked me about animals.

If the animal is fluffy, call the function is_fluffy. If the animal flies, call the function does_fly.
Do not answer the question. Do not say answer the question, just call one of these functions.
""",  # noqa: #501
        ),
        ("human", "{text}"),
    ]
)

off_topic_model = ChatOpenAI(model_name="gpt-3.5-turbo-0613").bind(
    functions=_build_no_arg_functions(
        [
            ("is_fluffy", "This should be called for fluffy animals"),
            ("does_fly", "This function should be called for animals that fly."),
        ]
    )
)

off_topic_chain = off_topic_prompt | off_topic_model #| AffirmOpenAIFunctionsAgentOutputParser()
```
![image](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/assets/62957343/5c36b45c-dab0-4e0f-9e19-57285d818e0d)

This behavior is not stable w.r.t. prompt. For example suppose I change the prompt to:

```
I will show you a question that someone asked me about animals. 

If the animal is fluffy, call the function is_fluffy. If the animal flies, call the function does_fly.
If the question is about an animal that neither flies nor is fluffy, answer the question. 

Do not answer the question. Do not say answer the question, just call one of these functions.
```
Then I get valid json in the return value.

![image](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/assets/62957343/7a0e424f-111c-42ba-96b7-bc6225fc943a)

body: Thanks for getting back to me! I can write up a test tomorrow to demonstrate the error, it I discovered it from ballooning context costs, it became more noticeable now that OpenAI models accept 16k context tokens. As for self.chat_memory.messages, I don't believe that's mutable, as the chat memory seems to be implemented as a BaseChatHistory, more so exposing any of the memory backends in memory/chat_message_histories rather than being able to write back to.
author: Jyumpp

body:
Got it. I'm actually seeing the right behavior when I follow the interface described in the docs https://python.langchain.com/docs/modules/memory/types/summary_buffer without this change.

Memory is in need of some work, so appreciate your attention to it! I would recommend using the interface as described in the docs to avoid infinitely accumulating messages though.
author: efriis

body: I respectfully disagree. While it does work with the default uninitialized memory, passing a premade history object, such as with the Postgres History chat_message_history loader, messages are not mutable.
author: Jyumpp

body: I've taken a pretty thorough reading of the memory source so far, and my team just submitted our research paper for our LLM framework for using these tools in a manufacturing setting to Manufacturing Letters, where actual persistent data stores are invaluable. If there are different pain points in memory you think should be addressed first, such as a possible other bug with the Postgres loader rather than this class, I'd be eager to put my time towards those instead. :)
author: Jyumpp

body:
Got it. Do you have code showing that bug? I didn't realize you were using it with something postgres related, and I could see that being an area ripe for bugs or questionable compatibility.

The main reason this PR shouldn't be merged is because it stores duplicate information in a new `chat_messages` attribute to `self.chat_memory.messages`
author: efriis

body:
My current code showing the bug is only our internal project, I can get the code cleaned up to push to our org repo to share plus a recreation test case. 

I agree the duplication is a bad idea. Instead, would it suffice to alter the ‘self.moving_summary_buffer‘ to be a tuple of the buffer string and the index of where ‘first_messages‘ ends?
author: Jyumpp

body:
I just pushed the work for our Discord bot to our org: [HERE](https://github.com/UGA-Innovation-Factory/AlfredBot/blob/main/alfred.py) 
- It requires 1 Postgres db, embeddings and chat logs stored in same db, different tables

I included 2 text files with the as_is langchain implementation, and the with_edit version that I'm using with the modifications, importing as a modified class in the project root dir.
author: Jyumpp

body:
Very interesting. Any interest in being one of the first users of our new Runnable-compatible memory? It landed today! https://python.langchain.com/docs/expression_language/how_to/message_history#adding-message-history

I think the main issue with the current approach is that BufferSummary memory doesn't support manually passing in the `chat_history` object as this code does.

Hey @Jyumpp ! This is the third time you've opened this PR, and I understand your frustration with the class. Would you be willing to try out the more up to date method of memory that I mentioned in #13481 ? https://python.langchain.com/docs/expression_language/how_to/message_history#adding-message-history

On this older memory object (`ConversationSummaryBufferMemory`):
In your PR description, you repeatedly reference the memory not functioning like you expect, but when I use the recommended interface documented in the docs, I don't see the behavior you see. As mentioned in #13481, I would guess this has to do with your code manually attaching a postgres-backed chat message history.

This code is unfortunately not mergeable because it would be a breaking change for people using it in the documented way (public attributes change type, return types of functions are different).

I'll leave this open to hear if you're ok to use the new one, but I'll probably close this afterwards!
author: efriis

body: Thanks for your time! I'll take a look at this new method, but that guide seems to indicate that it functions *only* on histories and not memories, which I think is more likely to bury the problem than solve it. I do feel that the ability to attach a reconstructed History object is important to many scenarios should they ever extend to prod tools rather than demo toys. To overcome this, would it be better to A) include a private member as the index rather than using the tuple method B) create a new summary buffer memory type exclusively for these immutable cases or C) suffice to just use patched code in projects that happen to run into this issue.

body:
Hi,

I can see two limitations resp. opportunities for improvement here:

1. using the local name of an IRI is not the intended way of providing a human readable name in RDF. The best practice is usually to use `rdfs:label` or similar properties (e.g. skos:prefLabel, skos:altLabel, ...). For example, in Wikidata all IRIs just have IDs like `https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q5`, same holds for many biomedical domain ontologies.
2. we should add a config option to restrict the text to a particular language, e.g. to English, Spanish, etc. - even if the LLM can handle different languages, in my opinion it'S way cleaner to have just one language per prompt. And in RDF you can indeed have `rdfs:comment` literals in multiple languages. The current code would therefore return multiple rows for the same class or property with descriptions in different languages. This would also make the prompt larger than necessary. 

I hope my comments make sense to some extent.

body:
I am getting an error when I am trying to load geodata using GeoDataFrameLoader with page_content_column='geometry'.
The issue lies in the package where it raises an error in this validation:
`if not isinstance(data_frame[page_content_column].iloc[0], gpd.GeoSeries):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected data_frame[{page_content_column}] to be a GeoSeries"
            )
`

here it is validating the `shapely.geometry.point.Point` with verified by `type(EventData['geometry'].iloc[0])`. To correct it you'd simply have to change 

`if not isinstance(data_frame[page_content_column], gpd.GeoSeries):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected data_frame[{page_content_column}] to be a GeoSeries"
            )
`

Thanks!

body:
Yes, it's needed. This issue is preventing me from trying out Gemini models in most of the tools I've built, which all require async streaming.

The lack of interest may be because most Langchain devs are in the US where it's possible to use the separate [Generative AI API](https://ai.google.dev/api/python/google/generativeai) to use Gemini. So Vertex support is somewhat neglected. 

That API is only available in [some regions](https://ai.google.dev/available_regions), with EU being a notable exception. In EU the only way to access Google's models is through Vertex.

author: thiagosalvatore

body:
@kofan @thiagosalvatore @jarib the main implementation of ChatVertexAI which now lives in the `langchain-google-vertexai` package (in the [langchain-google](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-google) repo) already implements async streaming
```python
from langchain_google_vertexai import ChatVertexAI

llm = ChatVertexAI(model_name="gemini-pro")
llm.astream(...)
```

closing this PR but let me know if you have any issues with the above!

and if helpful here are the ChatVertexAI [docs](https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/chat/google_vertex_ai_palm) and [API reference](https://api.python.langchain.com/en/latest/chat_models/langchain_google_vertexai.chat_models.ChatVertexAI.html#langchain_google_vertexai.chat_models.ChatVertexAI)
author: baskaryan

body:
@baskaryan Here is how the current implementation looks like:
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-google/blob/a13f3968239e53c3567a1ac0a6f23744f008ba4f/libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py#L436-L438
```python
 async def _agenerate(
        self,
        messages: List[BaseMessage],
        stop: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        run_manager: Optional[AsyncCallbackManagerForLLMRun] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> ChatResult:
        """Asynchronously generate next turn in the conversation.

        Args:
            messages: The history of the conversation as a list of messages. Code chat
                does not support context.
            stop: The list of stop words (optional).
            run_manager: The CallbackManager for LLM run, it's not used at the moment.

        Returns:
            The ChatResult that contains outputs generated by the model.

        Raises:
            ValueError: if the last message in the list is not from human.
        """
        if "stream" in kwargs:
            kwargs.pop("stream")
            logger.warning("ChatVertexAI does not currently support async streaming.")
```

body:
Moving LCEL up as the primary usage tool is legitimate. Still, we have `Agents` in this level but not `Chains`. I argue that `Chains` has the same, at least, importance as `Agents`. 
And LCEL is the `Language CHAIN Expression Language`, not LAEL, not LPEL. Chain is at the top of LangChain hierarchy. It is even on the logo. 🦜🔗 I'm not pushing up parrot yet. :) 
`Knight` maybe doesn't mean too much for now in the UK but it is respected. The same as the `Chain`.
author: leo-gan

body:
@leo-gan in practice, most of the chains are so application specific they are in use cases. The ones that arent are deprecated in favor of LCEL

For agents, the "Agents" sectoin can be thought of the equivalent of LCEL, but there are agent toolkits in the Use Case/Integration sections

body:
Issue in short, we're using the latest version of langchain with GCP product [Matching Engine](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/vector-search/overview) in a private VPC network design. However, it always hit error **object endpoint has no attribute "_public_match_client"** because we don't deploy the matching engine index to a public endpoint.

A quick fix for it is using "hasattr" to check the "endpoint" whether has attribute "_public_match_client".

body:
Although this can be solved, we found another issue. 

For the chat type of prompt, when **_message_list_** has only one _message_, `save()` and `load_prompt()` can run correctly. 

However, when **_message_list_** has more than one _message_, the role of the _message_ is not specified in the file saved by `save()`, and `load_prompt()` can only load the first _message_.

```python
from langchain.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
    [
        ("assistant", "hello"),
        ("human", "{query}"),
    ]
)
prompt.save("chat_template.json")
```

The result is as the following:

```
{
    "input_variables": [
        "query"
    ],
    "input_types": {},
    "output_parser": null,
    "partial_variables": {},
    "messages": [
        {
            "prompt": {
                "input_variables": [],
                "input_types": {},
                "output_parser": null,
                "partial_variables": {},
                "template": "hello",
                "template_format": "f-string",
                "validate_template": false,
                "_type": "prompt"
            },
            "additional_kwargs": {}
        },
        {
            "prompt": {
                "input_variables": [
                    "query"
                ],
                "input_types": {},
                "output_parser": null,
                "partial_variables": {},
                "template": "{query}",
                "template_format": "f-string",
                "validate_template": false,
                "_type": "prompt"
            },
            "additional_kwargs": {}
        }
    ],
    "validate_template": false,
    "_type": "chat"
}
```

Load the prompt from `chat_template.json`.

```
from langchain.chat_models import ErnieBotChat
from langchain.prompts import load_prompt

llm = ErnieBotChat()
prompt = load_prompt('chat_template.json')
print(prompt)
```

The result as the following:

```
input_variables=[] messages=[HumanMessagePromptTemplate(prompt=PromptTemplate(input_variables=[], template='hello'))]
```

body:
Hey @hinthornw! Resolved a good chunk of the suggestions! Wanted to hot-potato it before the weekend so I didn't have to worry about it for a few days, so no weekend rush or anything like that. 

Of note:
-  Took some creative liberties to try to compromise with the additional class options. Renamed them to much more general "GeneralChat/LLM", "CodeChat/LLM", "InstructChat/LLM", "ContextChat/LLM", "SteerChat/LLM", and "ImageChat/LLM". That way, users can safely drop these into their code and we can just swap out the defaults behind the scenes as better options come out. Also the model option is better-advertised and typical-use showcases are nicer now. I have checked and there is currently not a way to derive intake schemas from our API (i.e. does this model need labels, or context-only, or a sub-512-length max_tokens argument), so I think making these intuitive grouping classes is a good idea for now.
- I've confirmed some requirements for NeVA/Fuyu, and I think it's reasonable for us to incorporate; just need to be able to pull an image from user's local, resize to 336x336 (and yes, this kinda sucks for Fuyu at the moment; they're working on it), and toss it into a tag as you noted earlier. Do you have any recommendation for packages that would cause minimal problems for LC? (PIL ok?)
- Would love suggestions on how to let aembed_batch_<queries/documents> exist purely for pedagogical reasons. What do you think I could do to make it good enough? 

Thanks again, and have an awesome weekend! :D
author: VKudlay

body: @hinthornw @baskaryan Just to confirm, everything is good and the embedding model has been updated to add max concurrency restrictions. NeVA does not have deep incorporation yet (it's just a simple default-model class), but I've blocked off the ImageLLM/ImageChat abstraction for it and intend to update it with deeper incorporation (automatic image loading) later. If it will speed up the PR, we are happy to remove those classes for now. Regardless, things look good :D

body:
Our changes add the serialization and deserialization to and from the following memory types:
- `ConversationBufferWindowMemory`
- `ConversationBufferMemory`
- `ConversationSummaryBufferMemory`
- `ConversationSummaryMemory`
- `ConversationEntityMemory`
- `ConversationTokenBufferMemory`
For the following types an additional `llm` argument needs to be passed for deserialization, this is because the current BaseLLM class is not `lc_serializable`:
- `ConversationSummaryBufferMemory`
- `ConversationSummaryMemory`
- `ConversationEntityMemory`
- `ConversationTokenBufferMemory`
In the future, our implementation allows for extension to include Knowledge graphs and Vector Stores, if their `lc_serializable` methods are implemented to support both serialization and deserialization.
author: Aditya-k-23

body: We understand. We chose this issue as there were a lot of user requests for making storage of memory types available in a JSON format. We chose to couple it with deserialization because we thought it made sense to continue where users left off their work. We think this feature provides the capability to efficiently share, reuse, and manage memory objects across sessions and even with other users. To add a particular use case I would like to reference the issue #11275. Maybe @lameTookan can shed more light on what their use case was.
author: Aditya-k-23

body:
@hwchase17  Curious to hear - why the desire to have them serializable?

Currently building a system where each step in the conversation is produced by invoking a stateless API. So any conversation state must be passed in to the parameters used to invoke the API.

@Aditya-k-23 Why do these memory types require an llm to deserialize?

* ConversationSummaryBufferMemory
* ConversationSummaryMemory

For example, to my thinking the ConversationSummaryBufferMemory contains a list of Human and AI conversation steps, a current buffer size or token count, and maybe a summary of the conversation so far to capture the overflow from the buffer. A serialized representation could hold these 3 things, and the state could be completely recovered from them.

What we want to avoid is having to make extra calls to the llm to re-create the summary from the conversation steps when deserializing, as this is potentially costly/time consuming.

body: @amiaxys im stuggling to get tests to pass - any idea why?
author: hwchase17

body:
> @amiaxys im stuggling to get tests to pass - any idea why?

I think I mentioned it in the PR but basically, the Mongo database + agent tests pass since they use `tmp/mongodb-27017.sock` as an URI, which only exists when one has installed MongoDB locally, I believe. (We had to use Unix socket since all others were disabled when running `pytest`.) Since we didn't find a way to create unit tests that weren't superficial otherwise (we needed a legitimate URI and it appeared it was difficult to mock something as complex as MongoClient/Database), we just left it as is. 

We can remove them until a solution is figured out but I wasn't sure if it was an issue to have no unit tests showing that it worked, so I included the tests in PR for that reason. 

> Additionally, the tests pass locally due to having MongoDB installed since the tests use the `tmp/mongodb-27017.sock` Unix socket, but do not pass Github Actions test workflows for the same reason, and since we weren't sure whether it would be good practice to edit the workflow and haven't figured out a good way to mock PyMongo's MongoClient/Database that isn't unnecessarily complex or makes the unit tests superficial, we left it as is.

(We had to use Unix socket since all others were disabled when running `pytest`.) > 
> We can remove them until a solution is figured out but I wasn't sure if it was an issue to have no unit tests showing that it worked, so I included the tests in PR for that reason.
> 
> > Additionally, the tests pass locally due to having MongoDB installed since the tests use the `tmp/mongodb-27017.sock` Unix socket, but do not pass Github Actions test workflows for the same reason, and since we weren't sure whether it would be good practice to edit the workflow and haven't figured out a good way to mock PyMongo's MongoClient/Database that isn't unnecessarily complex or makes the unit tests superficial, we left it as is.

Hey, MongoDB employee here! 

Just taking a look at the failing actions test. It looks like those tests just need to spin up MongoDB via [supercharge/mongodb-github-action](https://github.com/supercharge/mongodb-github-action) in your current ci/langchain yml file. From there you can set the port, and should update the uri string in your test to match the new local mongo setup. Additionally, if you need a replica set, adding the `mongodb-replica-set` parameter will also help. Overall, the new snippet in Github Actions should look something like this: 

```
- name: MongoDB in GitHub Actions
   uses: supercharge/mongodb-github-action@1.10.0.
      with:
        mongodb-version: 7.0 // or whichever version needed
        mongodb-replica-set: test // or whichever name needed
        mongodb-port: 27017 // provided the default, but again whichever is needed
```

Highly recommend still reading through the marketplace action!

Let us know if that addition gets these tests to pass, if not, we're happy to assist in unblocking.

body: What does this accomplish that isn't possible through the HuggingFacePipeline class? This seems to be largely a copy but with a default model id, and we don't want to make new classes unless they are useful
author: hinthornw

body: Yes, I understand that making new classes that aren't useful and doesn't serve another purpose is not what we want. My group and I intention were to create an Agent for Starcoder in Langchain and this will be different than just the HuggingFacePipeline because it would allow developers to directly interact with Starcoder using the Agent. However, we so far have made the LLM custom class of Starcoder and are having difficultives coverting it into an Agent.
author: MarioLiao

body:
Hey @MarioLiao ! I don't think this will work as-is, and if you want to use this HuggingFace model in an agent, I'd recommend setting up your agent using the `HuggingFacePipeline` llm as described here, and recommended by @hinthornw : https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/llms/huggingface_pipelines

I'll close this because I don't think we want a specific LLM class for this model, which should be used via HuggingFacePipeline.

body: out of curiosity, what was the situation you were getting empty messages in?
author: baskaryan

body:
Hi @baskaryan,

By running the "RAG over code" example,
https://python.langchain.com/docs/use_cases/question_answering/code_understanding#chat

the parameter **return_messages** is set True as below
```
memory = ConversationSummaryMemory(
    llm=llm, memory_key="chat_history", return_messages=True
)

```
This triggers below logic
https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain/memory/summary.py#L70

Since **self.buffer** is empty at the very first turn, an empty "System Message" is built.
author: MarkYQJ

body:
> Hi @baskaryan,
> 
> By running the "RAG over code" example, https://python.langchain.com/docs/use_cases/question_answering/code_understanding#chat
> 
> the parameter **return_messages** is set True as below
> 
> ```
> memory = ConversationSummaryMemory(
>     llm=llm, memory_key="chat_history", return_messages=True
> )
> ```
> 
> This triggers below logic https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain/memory/summary.py#L70
> 
> Since **self.buffer** is empty at the very first turn, an empty "System Message" is built.

would it make more sense to update ConversationSummaryMemory to check if self.buffer is empty and return empty list if so (if return_messages=True)?

Absolutely, the base class for `Tongyi` has been updated to inherit from `BaseLLM`.

In addition:

- All linting issues have been addressed and resolved.
- The commits in this pull request have been consolidated into a single commit through squashing.

As of now, registering for [dashscope](https://dashscope.aliyun.com/) (Tongyi LLM online version) requires a mainland China phone number in order to obtain an [API](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/dashscope/developer-reference/api-details) Key. However, due to usage policies, I'm unable to share my personal API Key with you directly.

Nonetheless, I have conducted tests on all the `invoke`, `batch`, `stream`, `generate`, `__call__`,  and async-version methods and have not encountered any issues. I will continue to monitor for any related issues and address them as quickly as possible.

@hwchase17  please review the PR again, thank you.

`import os
import sys

import openai
from langchain.chains import ConversationalRetrievalChain, RetrievalQA
from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.document_loaders import DirectoryLoader, TextLoader
from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain.indexes import VectorstoreIndexCreator
from langchain.indexes.vectorstore import VectorStoreIndexWrapper
from langchain.llms import OpenAI
from langchain.vectorstores import Chroma

import constants

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = constants.APIKEY

PERSIST = False

query = None
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
  query = sys.argv[1]

if PERSIST and os.path.exists("persist"):
  print("Reusing index...\n")
  vectorstore = Chroma(persist_directory="persist", embedding_function=OpenAIEmbeddings())
  index = VectorStoreIndexWrapper(vectorstore=vectorstore)
else:
  loader = DirectoryLoader("data/")
  if PERSIST:
    index = VectorstoreIndexCreator(vectorstore_kwargs={"persist_directory":"persist"}).from_loaders([loader])
  else:
    index = VectorstoreIndexCreator().from_loaders([loader])

chain = ConversationalRetrievalChain.from_llm(
  llm=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"),
  retriever=index.vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 1}),
)

chat_history = []
while True:
  if not query:
    query = input("Prompt: ")
  if query in ['quit', 'q', 'exit']:
    sys.exit()
  result = chain({"question": query, "chat_history": chat_history})
  print(result['answer'])

  chat_history.append((query, result['answer']))
  query = None
`

body:
@efriis @hwchase17 
Thanks for this great contribution.
I'm with OCI Data and AI team, and I have one concern with the way this is organized, especially the fact that OCI has an official Gen AI Service and is working on contributing the classes for LLM and Embeddings in Langchain.
So you beat us to the punch there, which is appreciated, however you are using the generic model deployment endpoint, not the specific Gen AI endpoints. 
So in terms of the naming conventions, I would refrain from suffixing this work with xxxLLM as these are not LLM endpoints, and that would make it confusing to OCI users.
I think it should just be called BaseModelDeployment, XYZModelDeployment etc... and should support **kwargs so any param could be passed and made generic, and refrain from defining model specific classes. 
If you want to showcase using Llama2 deployed with this endpoint and using it for different use cases, that sounds great, however that should be part of a guide on how to use the ModelDeployment class / endpoints, as it seems like defining specific classes for this purpose and only exposing that in the docs greatly narrows the purpose of the ModelDeployment endpoint and will potentially clash with the official Gen AI service in the future.
Happy to discuss.

Our aim is to ensure they do not impact existing structures or naming conventions, thereby avoiding any backward compatibility issues.

author: efriis

body: @efriis OK Before, I also considered adding quarto [configuration file](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/scripts.html#pre-and-post-render) to solve the problem, namely `pre-render` and `post-render`, but in fact they also use additional scripts, and it is not easy to determine the source when a problem occurs. It is better to add it directly to in a bash script.

I did see another format problem, that is, the format displayed by docusaurus admonitions is incorrect. For [example](https://python.langchain.com/docs/expression_language/how_to/message_history#example-messages-input-dict-output): In the tips, the markdown url is not displayed accurately, there are several such links, but they are all displayed incorrectly. but it seems to be a bug in docusaurus.
Great catch! @bracesproul started work in #14349 it looks like

body:
how general is this? compared to being specific to how Walmart deploys LLMs internally?

My concern would be this makes some assumption about how you deploy LLMs that are not generalizable outside.

An alternative would be to maintain this as its own package, since it should just rely on langchain-core. this is actually how we will be moving most integrations in the future. if this is interesting, we're happy to help advise on this!
author: hwchase17
daichi-m

body:
It's unclear to me that this is sufficiently general. For instance we set
```python
json_body: Dict[str, Any] = {"prompt": prompt}
```
APIs would need to conform to this interface, right? And incorporating additional features may become unwieldy.

Closing for now, if there's interest we could move to `langchain-experimental`.
