body: @hwchase17 @efriis I have a small change I'm proposing within `langchain-core` over the `convert_to_secret_str` method.  The change I'm proposing allows this to accept a `None` and treat it as an empty string `""`. This makes it 1) consistent with the behavior of the `SecretStr` type from pydantic, 2) more compatible with the `api_key` types, which are usually typed as `Optional[str]`, and defaulting to `None`.
author: rancomp

body: @efriis this is a cleanup / standardization. Do you think it's still relevant?
author: rancomp

body:
Ah I think this actually bypasses an important part of type checking, where some classes may want to require that the passed in string is not None.

If you want to fix the case where it wasn't actually storing a masked SecretStr separately though, that would be great!
author: efriis

body:
> Ah I think this actually bypasses an important part of type checking, where some classes may want to require that the passed in string is not None.
> 
> If you want to fix the case where it wasn't actually storing a masked SecretStr separately though, that would be great!

I think there's confusion here. This PR:
- Still allows for the API-keys to be `None`
- Changes the way the SecretStr is extracted: Instead of casting `None` to `SecretStr` and then extracting the secret, the secret is extracted for `Union[SecretStr, str, None]` type all together through a single function.
- I made sure that all the classes use the `convert_to_secretstr` function (for standardization).

What I can also change is that the API-key type hint is changed to `Union[SecretStr, str, None]` instead of `Optional[str]` or `Optional[SecretStr]`.

What I can do is allow for the API-keys to be passed as `SecretStr` and not just `str`.

body:
The raw html *should* already exist in the documents you loaded from AsyncHtmlLoader. If you want to store the page content in your metadata, I would recommend just doing something like the following

```
from langchain.document_transformers import Html2TextTransformer
from langchain.document_loaders import AsyncHtmlLoader

urls = ["https://www.espn.com", "https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/"]
loader = AsyncHtmlLoader(urls)
docs = loader.load()

html2text = Html2TextTransformer()
docs_transformed = html2text.transform_documents(docs)

for d, dt in zip(docs, docs_transformed):
    dt.metadata["original_page"] = d.page_content
```

body:
Hey @efriis, nice to meet you, and thanks for reviewing this. I understand and agree with your rationale behind closing the proposed change.

Without making a backwards-incompatible change, we'd like to consolidate the GuardrailsOutputParser interface to just `from_guard`, that takes an already created `Guard` object as an argument. Guardrails' interface is still relatively fluid as it's in 0.x, we hope this will make it simpler to use different versions of Guardrails with Langchain.

I've updated the branch with this new classmethod, and deprecation warnings for the others. I don't think the PR is updating because it's closed though. Could you please reopen and review it? Thanks!

body:
@efriis 
It looks great. 
Still, several proposals from the current PR make sense:
-  "Core" is the first menu item, then "Langchain" 
- "Langchain", not "LangChain" (the capital "C" inside). Reason: namespaces are in the lower case. So, here the capitalization helps to visually separate one menu item from another. "LangChain" messes with this visual comprehension.
- "Docs" menu item is bold. It visually separates Docs from other menu items. Other menu items are linked to API Refernce, but Docs is linked to Documentation.

author: VKudlay

body: @VKudlay we're still working on better communicating it, but basically to better maintain the growing ecosystem, we're adding new integrations as separate packages that all depend on `langchain_core`, that way everything is compatible, and we'll still track it in the monorepo, but we can then improve the experience for communicating and managing dependencies, etc.
author: hinthornw

body:
@hinthornw Sounds good to me! Yeah, I read [the blogpost](https://blog.langchain.dev/the-new-langchain-architecture-langchain-core-v0-1-langchain-community-and-a-path-to-langchain-v0-1/) and can more-or-less see the vision.

It looks like at least one of our teams has already tried the new stuff, so looks like the changes are cool! I'm still gonna try it out as-is, but is it all good to go in its current state when the OSS stakeholders give the ok? Or are there any outstanding issues or things you want a second pair of eyes over first? :D

@efriis - Could you please comment on what needs to be done on this PR ?

> Hey there! Are all these methods in the vectorstore implementation necessary? There are a few nonstandard things going on here that will make this vectorstore difficult to use as well:
> 
>     * assumed dimensionality of openai embeddings -> does that need to be set on initialization?
> 
>     * documentation is missing - also how to run integration tests / set up a demo instance
> 
> 
> I'm going to close this PR for now, and if you add these, feel free to reopen! The lighter weight the implementation is here, the easier it will be to review.

I have followed pretty much the way `pgvector` vector store implementation was done. Could you please be more elaborate on what is non-standard here ? I am sorry but I am doing this the first time and not sure which one to follow as a reference.
